@oh-my-pi/pi-natives

Fixed
  • Fixed omp 18.4.3 and later crashing with a segmentation fault at startup on Apple silicon Macs running macOS older than 27; Apple Foundation Models support now loads only on macOS 27 and later

@oh-my-pi/pi-tui

Added
  • Added an optional terminal section to theme JSON (background, foreground, chrome, widget, 16 ansi colors) naming the terminal a theme was made for, for hosts that paint the terminal themselves; the built-in themes ported from known schemes (GitHub, Nord, Dracula, Catppuccin, Solarized, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night, One, Monokai, Rosé Pine, Poimandres, Celestial) carry their scheme's.
Fixed
  • Fixed native-terminal (TSP) frames held back by unacknowledged credits waiting for an unrelated render after the 5-second stall fallback expired; a credit-blocked change now renders as soon as the oldest frame counts as stalled.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/compare/v18.4.7...v18.4.8

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 27, 2026
lovable.summary: Events & hooks for your workspace Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans can now extend their workspace with their own services using Events & Hooks. Events notify your HTTPS endpoint when a project is created, published, transferred to…
lovable.html:
Events & hooks for your workspace

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans can now extend their workspace with their own services using Events & Hooks. Events notify your HTTPS endpoint when a project is created, published, transferred to another workspace, or deleted. Hooks let your endpoint allow or block an action first, such as checking a message sent in a project's chat for sensitive data before Lovable processes it. Find it in your workspace settings.

Connect your app to Scrive

You can now connect your Lovable app to Scrive for e-signatures and electronic identification (eID). Scrive eSign sends documents for signature and tracks their signing status. Scrive eID Hub verifies who your app's users are with national eIDs such as BankID and MitID. It fits contract sending portals, onboarding with signed agreements, and identity-verified sign-ups. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Redesigned sidebar

The sidebar now organizes your projects and chats into three sections: Pinned, Projects, and Recent chats. Pinned replaces Starred and shows the projects and chats you pinned, with the most recently pinned first. Projects and Recent chats each link to their full list.

Knowledge is now Instructions

In workspace and project settings, Knowledge is now Instructions. Workspace knowledge and project knowledge are now called workspace instructions and project instructions. They work the same way, so nothing changes for your projects.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 26, 2026
lovable.summary: Manage IdP group mappings in one place Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans now map IdP groups to workspace roles in the Provisioning groups section of the workspace's Identity settings. On Enterprise plans, SCIM provisioning uses the…
lovable.html:
Manage IdP group mappings in one place

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans now map IdP groups to workspace roles in the Provisioning groups section of the workspace's Identity settings. On Enterprise plans, SCIM provisioning uses the same mappings. Workspace owners can also map a group to the Owner role.

Redesigned connector pages

Each connector's page now has a Connect button that creates the first connection type the connector supports. More options lists the other types. The connector's connections appear in one Connections list, where the Visibility column shows whether each one is Private or Shared. You can sort the list by name, visibility, or number of projects.

Scroll through all files in the Files tab

Your project's Files tab now loads more files as you scroll, so you can browse a large project's files in one list.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 22, 2026
lovable.summary: Clearer Privacy & security settings The Privacy & security settings have reworded labels and descriptions that say what each setting controls. Changes with a wide effect, such as enabling automatic deletion of abandoned projects or restricting code downloads,…
lovable.html:
Clearer Privacy & security settings

The Privacy & security settings have reworded labels and descriptions that say what each setting controls. Changes with a wide effect, such as enabling automatic deletion of abandoned projects or restricting code downloads, now open a confirmation dialog that shows what the change does. The change applies after you confirm. Three settings have new names: Default website access is now Default published app access, External invites is now External viewer invites, and the Security automation section is now Security checks.

Folder access applies to personal folders only

When a personal folder becomes a workspace folder, the access levels you granted stop applying to the projects inside it. The people and groups you invited keep their workspace role and any access you gave them on a project directly.

Gemini 2.5 chat models are retired for your app's AI features

The Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite chat models (google/gemini-2.5-pro, google/gemini-2.5-flash, and google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite) are no longer available for your app's AI features. They retired on October 20, 2026. Your app's requests for Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash now go to Gemini 3.8 Flash, and requests for Flash Lite go to Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite. Your app keeps working without a code change, but the replacement can cost a different amount per request and respond differently. If your app uses one of these models, ask Lovable to switch it to a current model.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 21, 2026
lovable.summary: See adoption by department without SCIM Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans can now see adoption by department in Insights when your workspace uses SSO without SCIM. To set it up, map the department attribute in your SAML or OIDC app.…
lovable.html:
See adoption by department without SCIM

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans can now see adoption by department in Insights when your workspace uses SSO without SCIM. To set it up, map the department attribute in your SAML or OIDC app. Lovable then reads it at each sign-in, so the breakdown fills as your members return.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 20, 2026
lovable.summary: Group your workspaces into an organization Enterprise companies that run several Lovable workspaces can now manage them together in an organization. The company sets up SSO once for all of them, and with SCIM the identity provider adds and removes members…
lovable.html:
Group your workspaces into an organization

Enterprise companies that run several Lovable workspaces can now manage them together in an organization. The company sets up SSO once for all of them, and with SCIM the identity provider adds and removes members automatically. Org admins see every member and role in one place, and teams can publish internal apps to everyone in the company. Each workspace keeps its own projects, members, groups, and billing. Lovable sets this up on request through your account team.

Let Lovable create your Supabase project

You can now ask Lovable to create a Supabase project for an app that has no backend. You choose the organization and the region, and Lovable creates the project there and connects it to your app. This works in workspaces where the built-in backend is disabled. A project's region cannot be changed later, and Supabase bills the new project to your own organization.

App + chat connectors: LlamaParse Platform and n8n

LlamaParse Platform lets apps parse documents and extract structured data from them, such as the parties and dates in a contract. Use it for document review tools, knowledge base assistants, and apps that read the files your users upload. With Managed by Lovable, parsing and extraction spend workspace credits.

n8n lets apps list workflows, read executions, trigger webhooks, and publish or unpublish workflows on your n8n instance. Use it for internal consoles, intake forms, and status pages built on workflows you already run.

Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Seedream 5 Pro and Seedance 2.5 for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now use two new ByteDance models:

  • Seedream 5 Pro (bytedance/seedream-5-pro) generates and edits images from a text prompt and up to 10 reference images, for posters, ads, and designs. It renders text inside the image accurately.
  • Seedance 2.5 (bytedance/seedance-2.5) generates 4 to 30 second video clips with synchronized sound, at 480p or 720p. It takes reference images, video, and audio, and can edit and extend an existing clip.

Workspace admins and owners enable ByteDance in Connectors first. Ask Lovable to use either model in your app.

Redesigned More menu

The More menu now lists your project's services directly in the sidebar: Database, Users, Storage, Emails, and Usage. Agent integrations is grouped under AI, and Secrets under Settings. The SQL editor, Edge functions, and Jobs are in the Database view, under Manage.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 19, 2026
lovable.summary: Connect your app to Cube You can now connect your Lovable app to Cube to read the measures and dimensions your data team defines in its semantic layer, on Cube Cloud or on a Cube Core instance you host yourself. It fits dashboards, reports, and internal tools…
lovable.html:
Connect your app to Cube

You can now connect your Lovable app to Cube to read the measures and dimensions your data team defines in its semantic layer, on Cube Cloud or on a Cube Core instance you host yourself. It fits dashboards, reports, and internal tools built on the metrics your company already agrees on. The connection is read-only. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Faster dictation

Dictation now transcribes while you speak, so your text is ready when you stop recording. It works in the project chat, in Chats, on the create form, and in the mobile apps.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 18, 2026
lovable.summary: Request edit access to a project you can only view You can now ask for edit access without leaving the project. Select Request to edit at the top of the project and add an optional message. Lovable emails the project's owner, or the workspace's admins and…
lovable.html:
Request edit access to a project you can only view

You can now ask for edit access without leaving the project. Select Request to edit at the top of the project and add an optional message. Lovable emails the project's owner, or the workspace's admins and owners, who can approve or deny the request.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 17, 2026
lovable.summary: Request a higher workspace role Workspace viewers and editors can now request a higher role from the People tab. Viewers can ask for editor or admin access, and editors for admin access, each with an optional reason. You can withdraw a request while it is…
lovable.html:
Request a higher workspace role

Workspace viewers and editors can now request a higher role from the People tab. Viewers can ask for editor or admin access, and editors for admin access, each with an optional reason. You can withdraw a request while it is pending. Workspace admins and owners approve or deny it. Admin access requires a paid workspace plan.

Jump to your last chat in the desktop app

In the Lovable desktop app, tap Ctrl+Tab to switch to the chat you were in before. Hold Ctrl and press Tab to pick from your recent chats instead, with the chat you are in first. The shortcut uses Ctrl on macOS as well.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 16, 2026
lovable.summary: Require approval or block publishing with workspace policies Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now set workspace policies that block publishing or require an admin or owner to approve it first. Policies cover apps with unresolved findings of…
lovable.html:
Require approval or block publishing with workspace policies

Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now set workspace policies that block publishing or require an admin or owner to approve it first. Policies cover apps with unresolved findings of personal data, apps published by external collaborators, apps published publicly, apps that use connectors, and publishing from unverified email domains. When a policy requires approval, the person publishing sends a request from the publish dialog, and Lovable publishes the app when an admin or owner approves it. Enable policies in your workspace's Privacy & security settings.

Review publish requests and findings in the Action center

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans now have an Action center in the dashboard sidebar. It lists what needs a decision: publish requests waiting for approval, projects whose owner left the workspace, projects whose credit usage rose sharply, public apps with critical security findings, and public apps with no edits for months. From each row you can approve or deny a request, assign an owner, or unpublish an app.

Add OIDC sign-in to your app

In an app on the built-in backend (Cloud), you can now let your users sign in with your own OpenID Connect provider, such as Auth0, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, or Keycloak, next to the other sign-in methods. Enable OIDC in your project's authentication settings and enter the details from your provider. Lovable then starts a build that adds the sign-in button to your app. The build is treated as standard build usage and consumes credits. Sign-ins consume no credits.

Lovable writes and runs tests for the rules you change

Lovable now adds a small test when you add or change a rule in your app, such as a price, a limit, or a permission. It runs the tests that cover the change before it reports the work as done, and keeps the tests in your project. Lovable does not write tests for copy, styling, or markup.

Connect your app to Pledge

You can now connect your Lovable app to Pledge to search verified nonprofits worldwide, create and track donations, and create and update fundraisers. It fits donation checkouts, loyalty point redemption, cause campaign pages, and employee giving programs. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

GPT Transcribe for your app's speech-to-text features

Your app's AI features can now use OpenAI's GPT Transcribe (openai/gpt-transcribe), the new default speech-to-text model. It accepts audio files up to 25 MB, and your app can pass context, expected keywords, and languages as hints for names and specialist vocabulary. Ask Lovable to use it in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick.

Formatted Markdown previews in the Files tab

Markdown files in your project's Files tab now open as formatted text, with tables, task lists, footnotes, and code blocks you can copy. Markdown files in Chats open in the same preview.

Larger document previews in the Files tab

A document you open in your project's Files tab now fills the preview pane. Its actions, such as adding it to the chat or a collection, are in the header above the document.

Removed: tabs in the desktop app

Tabs have been removed from the Lovable desktop app in version 1.9. The sidebar already lists your chats and projects, so the tabs were redundant. Switch between chats and projects from the sidebar, or hold Ctrl+Tab to pick from your recent chats. New downloads include 1.9, and the app offers the update when you open it.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 15, 2026
lovable.summary: Export audit logs to your SIEM or cloud storage Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now schedule exports of the workspace's audit logs to Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, Splunk, or Azure Log Analytics. Lovable delivers new…
lovable.html:
Export audit logs to your SIEM or cloud storage

Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now schedule exports of the workspace's audit logs to Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, Splunk, or Azure Log Analytics. Lovable delivers new events every hour or every 3 hours, so you can keep an audit trail for longer than the 13 weeks Lovable stores it and search Lovable activity next to your other security events. Find it under Workspace settings → Security → Data exports. Data exports come at no extra charge from Lovable. Your destination provider bills you for storage and ingestion.

Use Lovable from Claude through your company's SSO

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans can now enable enterprise-managed authentication, so members use the Lovable MCP server in Claude with their Okta identity, without a separate Lovable sign-in. Enable it in your workspace's Identity settings and pick the SSO provider your team already uses. Members keep their existing workspace and project permissions. Claude requires a Team or Enterprise plan.

Login pages include Sign in with Lovable by default

Login pages that Lovable builds for an app with Lovable Cloud now include Sign in with Lovable by default, alongside email and password sign-in and Google sign-in. Your app's users can sign in with their Lovable account, and Lovable registers the sign-in for your project with nothing to configure. To use a different set of methods, name them in your prompt. Sign-ins consume no credits.

GPT-6.1 Sol for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now use OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol (openai/gpt-6.1-sol), a model for complex coding and professional work. It accepts text and image input and responds with text. Ask Lovable to use it in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick.

Documents in the project chat show their name and type

Documents that Lovable creates or refers to in a project chat reply now appear as a list with each file's name and a file-type icon, separate from the preview grid for images and videos. A single document with a preview, such as a PDF or a Markdown file, appears as a larger preview card. Select a row or card to open the file in the Files tab.

Select and sort files faster in the Files tab

In your project's Files tab, you can now select several files by hovering over a file and selecting its checkbox, then add them to the chat or a collection, download them, or delete them. Inside a collection, you can now sort files by Updated, Name, or Size, and the sort button shows which field is active. In list view, each document shows a file-type icon.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 14, 2026
lovable.summary: Growth tools: from building your app to growing it Lovable now helps you find customers, from the same chat where you build. Set a goal such as "my first 100 signups", and Growth tools turn it into a plan built from your app, your audience, and your traffic.…
lovable.html:
Growth tools: from building your app to growing it

Lovable now helps you find customers, from the same chat where you build. Set a goal such as "my first 100 signups", and Growth tools turn it into a plan built from your app, your audience, and your traffic. Lovable tells you what to fix first, and says so when ads are premature.

  • Growth advice that knows your app. Lovable recommends your next move: help search engines and AI assistants find your app, sharpen the offer on your landing page, prepare posts and listings for the communities, directories, and creators that reach your audience, or set up a Google Business Profile for a local business.
  • Ads launched from Lovable. Create a new Google Ads account or connect an existing one, and use your Facebook account for ads on Facebook and Instagram. Lovable sets up tracking and creates campaigns on Google, YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram. You decide the ad budget and approve when spending can start.
  • Creative built from your app. Ask for a launch video, an animated product demo, a video ad, images, or ad copy that match your brand, ready for a campaign, a social post, or customer outreach.

Results show in the redesigned Analytics view: visits by channel, campaign results on the Ads tab, and a Get more visitors button that sends your current traffic to Lovable with your request. Lovable adds no extra fees for using Growth tools, and the standard costs of chatting with Lovable apply. Google or Meta charges the payment method on your advertising account for the ads you run.

Add Sign in with Lovable to any website

You can now let people sign in to your website with their Lovable account, including a site you did not build with Lovable. Add one script tag and a button, and your site receives the person's name, email address, and picture, depending on which of those you ask for. If your site has a server, you can use the standard OpenID Connect flow in place of the script. Both paths start from an OAuth client registered in your workspace settings. Sign-ins consume no credits.

Connect your apps to Lovable with OAuth

Workspace admins and owners can now register OAuth clients under Workspace settings → API keys & OAuth → OAuth clients. An OAuth client lets your app ask each user to allow access to their profile, projects, or workspaces, and gives you a client ID and, for a Web server client, a client secret. Sensitive scopes, which read or change projects and workspaces, require a Business or Enterprise plan and verification from Lovable. Users see a warning until the client is verified.

Let your app's users sign in with their Lovable account

In an app with Lovable Cloud, you can now let your users sign in with their Lovable account. Enable it in your project's auth settings, or ask Lovable in the project chat to add the button. Lovable registers the sign-in for your project and keeps it current when your app's address changes. Your app receives each user's name, email address, and profile picture, and the consent screen shows your project's name. Sign-ins consume no credits.

Ask Lovable what drives your run credit usage

You can now ask Lovable what drives run credit usage in the project chat. Lovable reads the recorded usage, investigates the app's scheduled jobs, functions, database, storage, and AI activity, traces what it finds to the project's code, and proposes fixes. Lovable makes a change only when you ask for it. Workspace admins and owners can also ask in Chats which projects and usage categories drive the whole workspace's run credit usage.

From the usage chart, workspace admins and owners can start the same investigation with Optimize your usage. The button appears below the chart in Usage details and in a project's Cloud usage view when the workspace or project used more than 5 run credits in the last 7 days. In Usage details, it starts a workspace-wide investigation in Chats. In a project, it starts the investigation in the project chat, in Chat mode, where Lovable does not edit your project's code.

Connect your app to Bing Webmaster Tools

You can now connect your Lovable app to Bing Webmaster Tools to read clicks, impressions, top queries, and crawl stats for the sites verified in your Bing Webmaster Tools account, and to submit URLs and sitemaps. It fits search dashboards, crawl monitors, and tools that send new pages or feeds to Bing. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Restore a deleted project yourself

You can now restore a deleted project for 60 days after you delete it. Select Restore under Recently deleted projects in your workspace settings. The project returns with its code, version history, and chat history, and a paused Cloud backend resumes. You can restore the projects you own. Workspace owners can restore every deleted project in the workspace, whoever deleted it. After 60 days, the project is permanently deleted.

Restore a deleted workspace yourself

Workspace owners on Free, Pro, and Business plans can now restore a deleted workspace, with its projects and members, for 60 days after deleting it. Select Restore under Recently deleted workspaces in your account settings. If the workspace's subscription ended while it was deleted, the workspace returns on the Free plan. After 60 days, the workspace is permanently deleted.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 13, 2026
lovable.summary: Let browser agents use your app You can now let browser agents use your app. When you enable agent integrations, Lovable also adds WebMCP tools to your app, so an AI agent built into the browser can act on the page a person has open, such as marking a task as…
lovable.html:
Let browser agents use your app

You can now let browser agents use your app. When you enable agent integrations, Lovable also adds WebMCP tools to your app, so an AI agent built into the browser can act on the page a person has open, such as marking a task as done or filtering a list. Browser tools run in the person's own browser tab with their signed-in session, separate from your app's MCP server, and you can also ask Lovable in the project chat to add them without a server. Lovable starts with tools that read information or are easy to undo, and adds tools that delete, pay, send, publish, or share only when you ask.

Gemini 4 Argon for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now use Google's Gemini 4 Argon (google/gemini-4-argon), a frontier model for long-horizon coding, reasoning, and knowledge work. It accepts text, image, audio, and video input and comes at a premium price. Ask Lovable to use it in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick.

Approve every tool from a chat connector at once

You can now select Always allow all tools from this connection when Lovable asks you to approve a tool from a chat connector, and every tool from that connection runs without asking from then on, including tools the server adds later. The choice applies to your own approvals only, and you can change it in the connection's settings in Connectors.

Supported PostgreSQL extensions on Lovable Cloud

Lovable Cloud databases support a fixed set of PostgreSQL extensions, such as pg_cron, pg_net, vector, and postgis. Lovable now refuses CREATE EXTENSION for any other extension, in the project chat, the SQL editor, and the Lovable API, and builds the feature with plain SQL instead. Extensions already installed in your database keep working.

Search for individual settings

You can now search for individual settings in workspace settings. Start typing in the search box at the top of the settings sidebar, and the results list the matching settings grouped by settings page, with the matching words highlighted. Select a result to open that setting.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 12, 2026
lovable.summary: Edit images directly in the Files tab You can now mark a change directly on an image in your project's Files tab. Open the image and select Edit, then draw over an area and describe the change, pin a comment where you want something changed, erase what you…
lovable.html:
Edit images directly in the Files tab

You can now mark a change directly on an image in your project's Files tab. Open the image and select Edit, then draw over an area and describe the change, pin a comment where you want something changed, erase what you want removed, or remove the background. Lovable saves the result as a new file next to the original.

See how much usage your free allowances cover

On Free, Pro, and Business plans, you can now see how much of your usage the free allowances covered. Usage details shows the covered credits next to the total above the chart, and the By coverage view splits each bar into what the daily build credits, the daily chat allowance, and the monthly Cloud, AI, and connector grants paid for, and what drew on your general credits.

Connect your app to Loops

You can now connect your Lovable app to Loops to create and update contacts, send events that start your Loops automations, and send transactional email you manage in Loops. It fits waitlists, signup forms, and product notifications that should reach people from your Loops audience. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 9, 2026
lovable.summary: Publish every app in your workspace under your own domain Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now set a publishing domain for the workspace, so projects publish at your-app.yourdomain.com instead of your-app.lovable.app. Pick a domain you…
lovable.html:
Publish every app in your workspace under your own domain

Workspace admins and owners on Enterprise plans can now set a publishing domain for the workspace, so projects publish at your-app.yourdomain.com instead of your-app.lovable.app. Pick a domain you bought through Lovable, or a subdomain of it, with no DNS setup. You can also connect a domain or subdomain you own elsewhere. Each project moves to the new address the next time you publish it, and its existing lovable.app address keeps working. Find it under Workspace settings → Workspace domains → Publishing domain.

Reference another chat or send it a task

In Chats, you can now work with your other chats. Reference a chat to let Lovable read what you discussed there, or ask Lovable to send a message to another chat or to start a new chat with a first task. Type @ and select the chat under Chats, or paste a link to the chat. The other chat does the work and can reply in your conversation, so one chat can coordinate several others.

Generate a secret that another app also needs

When Lovable asks you for a secret that you enter in two places, such as the secret GitHub uses to sign its webhook requests or a token two of your apps share, the secret form now has a Generate button. Select it to fill in a strong random value, copy the value to the other place, and submit. Lovable shows the value only in the form, and does not repeat stored secret values, or anything derived from them, in the project chat, in logs, or in your code.

Buy .si domains through Lovable

You can now buy .si domains, the Slovenian country-code extension, through Lovable. Search for the full name including the extension from Buy a domain in your project's or workspace's domain settings. A new .si domain can take up to 2 hours to start working, and you can register it for up to 5 years.

Get a warning before your credits run out

On Free, Pro, and Business plans, workspace admins and owners now get a warning when the workspace is likely to run out of credits before its monthly credits refill. The warning appears on the Plans & credit usage page and in Usage details, shows when your credits are expected to run out and when your monthly credits refill, and lets you add credits before your published apps are affected.

Enterprise credit balances now appear as numbers

On Enterprise plans, the credit panel on the Plans & credit usage page now shows your balance as numbers in place of a progress bar. Admins and owners see how many workspace credits remain and the workspace total, for example 6,400 remaining of 10,000. When the workspace has used more than its commitment, they also see a warning and an Overage credits row. Other members see only their own personal credits.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 8, 2026
lovable.summary: Publish to invited people only on Free and Pro plans On Free and Pro plans, you can now publish your app to an invite-only audience. In the publish dialog, select Invite only, then add workspace members by name or invite people outside your workspace by email.…
lovable.html:
Publish to invited people only on Free and Pro plans

On Free and Pro plans, you can now publish your app to an invite-only audience. In the publish dialog, select Invite only, then add workspace members by name or invite people outside your workspace by email. Only the people you add can visit the published app, after logging in, along with the project owner, workspace owners, and people the project is shared with directly. Publishing to your whole workspace or to groups still requires a Business or Enterprise plan.

App + chat connectors: Zendesk, Neon, MotherDuck, Oracle Autonomous AI Database, IBM Db2, Qlik Cloud, Omni, Metabase, and GoodData

Nine new app + chat connectors let your apps work with your help desk, your own databases, and the metrics your team defines in a business intelligence tool. Add them from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect one.

  • Manage Zendesk support tickets from your app. Zendesk lets apps read, create, and update support tickets, look up users and organizations, and read help center articles.
  • Query your own database from your app:
    • Neon lets apps read and write your own Neon Postgres database with SQL.
    • MotherDuck lets apps run DuckDB SQL on your MotherDuck databases and shares.
    • Oracle Autonomous AI Database lets apps run SQL on your Oracle Autonomous AI Database, including the Oracle Fusion ERP and HCM data that Fusion Data Intelligence stores there.
    • IBM Db2 lets apps run SQL on Db2 on Cloud.
  • Show your team's BI metrics in your app:
    • Qlik Cloud lets apps browse your Qlik apps, export chart and table data, ask Insight Advisor questions, and start reloads.
    • Omni lets apps query the topics and measures your team defines in Omni and draw their own charts from the results.
    • Metabase lets apps run saved Metabase questions and custom queries against the databases connected to Metabase, on Metabase Cloud or a self-hosted instance.
    • GoodData lets apps read the workspaces, metrics, and saved visualizations in GoodData Cloud and compute reports from them.
Chat connectors: Loom

Loom is now available as a prebuilt chat connector, so Lovable can read a Loom video's transcript, AI summary, and comments while you build. Paste a Loom link in the project chat to show Lovable a bug or an idea instead of describing it. Add it from Connectors.

Removed: design directions before the first build

The three design directions Lovable showed before building a visually open-ended prompt have been removed. Lovable now builds the look directly from what you describe, and still asks design questions about color, typography, and layout when your prompt leaves the look open. Older chats keep the direction you picked, without the previews.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 7, 2026
lovable.summary: Set credit usage limits and alerts for your workspace Workspace admins and owners on paid plans can now set usage limits and alerts that keep shared credits under control. Set a credit threshold for the whole workspace, a project, a member, or, on Business and…
lovable.html:
Set credit usage limits and alerts for your workspace

Workspace admins and owners on paid plans can now set usage limits and alerts that keep shared credits under control. Set a credit threshold for the whole workspace, a project, a member, or, on Business and Enterprise plans, a group or an access token, and choose what happens when usage reaches it: an email or in-app alert, or a block that stops building or pauses Lovable Cloud, AI features, and metered connector requests in deployed apps. You can also get an alert when your workspace balance drops below an amount or percentage you choose, and members who reach a blocking limit can request an increase that you approve or deny. Find it under Workspace settings → Usage limits & alerts.

Get help when your Cloud database is under high load

When your Lovable Cloud database runs low on resources, Lovable can now warn you that your app is under high load in the project chat, in the Publish dialog, and in More → Cloud → Database. Click Resolve to have Lovable check whether the database is still under pressure, find the likely cause, and suggest query or code changes before you move to a larger instance. When a larger instance is the right fix, Lovable shows the credit impact and offers the resize for your approval. Resizing from chat is available on paid plans.

Cloud database changes are now recorded as Drizzle migrations

When Lovable changes the structure of your Lovable Cloud database, it now records each change as a migration file in your project's code, under drizzle/migrations/. Lovable uses Drizzle, an open-source tool for database migrations, to create and apply these files. A migration file is a SQL file that describes one change to the database structure, so your code carries the full history of how your database was built. Lovable also refuses changes that could break your published app, such as dropping or renaming a table or column, and reaches the same result by adding to your database instead, for example by adding a new column and copying the data over. To let Lovable make such changes directly, set Execute backward incompatible database migrations in your Cloud permissions.

Faster inline text edits

Simple text changes you make with Edit text inline in the preview toolbar now apply in a few seconds. Text that your app builds from data or translates still takes a little longer.

Gemini 3.7 Flash is deprecated for your app's AI features

Google is retiring Gemini 3.7 Flash (google/gemini-3.7-flash), so it is now marked deprecated for your app's AI features and stops working on January 28, 2027. Apps that use it keep working until then, and Lovable no longer picks it for new AI features. If your app uses it, ask Lovable to switch to Gemini 3.8 Flash (google/gemini-3.8-flash) before that date.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 6, 2026
lovable.summary: Connect your app to Klaviyo You can now connect your Lovable app to Klaviyo to look up and update customer profiles, subscribe people to a list when they give email or SMS consent, record events such as signups and purchases, and read your campaigns and flows.…
lovable.html:
Connect your app to Klaviyo

You can now connect your Lovable app to Klaviyo to look up and update customer profiles, subscribe people to a list when they give email or SMS consent, record events such as signups and purchases, and read your campaigns and flows. It fits newsletter signup forms, SMS opt-in forms, and internal pages that show campaign status. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Chat connectors: Excalidraw+

Excalidraw+ is now available as a prebuilt chat connector, so Lovable can list, search, and edit the scenes in your Excalidraw+ workspace while you build, including diagrams, wireframes, and presentations. Add it from Connectors.

Connect to Databricks with your own account

The Databricks connector now lets you connect by signing in with your own Databricks account instead of a service principal. Select User OAuth when you create the connection. Queries run as you, so your own Unity Catalog permissions apply and Databricks audit logs show who ran each query.

Redesigned model list for the built-in AI connector

The AI connector in Connectors now lists every model your app's AI features can use as a card with its name, provider, a short description, and what it does. Search the list by model name, provider, or capability.

Gemini 3.6 Flash is deprecated for your app's AI features

Google is retiring Gemini 3.6 Flash (google/gemini-3.6-flash), so it is now marked deprecated for your app's AI features and stops working on November 19, 2026. Apps that use it keep working until then, and Lovable no longer picks it for new AI features. If your app uses it, ask Lovable to switch to Gemini 3.8 Flash (google/gemini-3.8-flash) before that date.

lovable.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 5, 2026
lovable.summary: Lyria 3 music models for your app's AI features Your app's AI features can now generate music with two Google models, from a text prompt or an image, with vocals or as an instrumental: Lyria 3 Clip Preview, for clips of about 30 seconds. Lyria 3 Pro Preview,…
lovable.html:
Lyria 3 music models for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now generate music with two Google models, from a text prompt or an image, with vocals or as an instrumental:

  • Lyria 3 Clip Preview, for clips of about 30 seconds.
  • Lyria 3 Pro Preview, for full tracks up to 184 seconds.

Ask Lovable to use either model in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick. Generating music uses credits, charged per finished track and only when a generation succeeds.

App + chat connectors: beehiiv and Ramp

beehiiv lets apps add subscribers, show posts from your publication, and save draft posts. Use it for signup forms, post listings, and launch waitlists for a newsletter you already run.

Ramp lets apps read the transactions, cards, funds and spending limits, users, and business information of your Ramp business. Use it for spend dashboards, transaction reporting, and card and limit inventories.

Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Restore Lovable work after a push to your Git repository replaces it

You can now restore work Lovable made after a push to your synced repository replaces it. Lovable saves a backup first and shows a notice in the editor and in Project settings → Git, where the project owner restores the saved work or keeps the repository's version. Restored work syncs back to your repository, or to a lovable-sync branch when the repository has newer commits.

• Store chats in per-chat cache files with a lazy-loaded index instead of one whole-workspace blob, fixing CPU spikes and slow startup as history grows; legacy caches migrate automatically. #557

  • Hooks db_cache_path now points at the workspace cache dir instead of db.transit.json; read-chat --db-cache-path accepts the dir or a legacy file. #557

  • Keep compact_chat in the tool schema across normal and compact requests, preserving prompt-cache prefixes while rejecting calls outside active compaction.

  • Provide token metrics for ollama provider. #567.

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.152.0
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Share chat history across git worktrees of the same repo, and merge workspace cache writes from concurrent servers instead of overwriting. #558 Cache models.dev catalog on disk and fall back to it when the fetch fails, avoiding model capabilities silently…
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html:
• Share chat history across git worktrees of the same repo, and merge workspace cache writes from concurrent servers instead of overwriting. #558
  • Cache models.dev catalog on disk and fall back to it when the fetch fails, avoiding model capabilities silently degrading (e.g. no image input) on transient network failures.
  • Fix ChatGPT OAuth routing and Responses Lite payloads for GPT-5.6 models. #563
  • Retry overloaded OpenAI post-tool requests without rerunning completed tools. #563

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.151.1
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Fix git tool heredoc failures for messages with apostrophes on old shells (e.g. macOS bash 3.2); git tool now honors toolCall.shellCommand path/args config. #562
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html: • Fix git tool heredoc failures for messages with apostrophes on old shells (e.g. macOS bash 3.2); git tool now honors toolCall.shellCommand path/args config. #562

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.151.0
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Return exhausted provider errors and partial output from sub-agents instead of reporting successful empty results. Add provider retry config for retry counts, backoff, and chat recovery; no-output retries replay the original request. Fail fast with the…
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html:
• Return exhausted provider errors and partial output from sub-agents instead of reporting successful empty results.
  • Add provider retry config for retry counts, backoff, and chat recovery; no-output retries replay the original request.
  • Fail fast with the resolved path when a hook action file doesn't exist; document that relative hook file paths resolve against the first workspace root.
  • Fix OpenAI Responses SSE errors, incomplete responses, and premature stream closes so chats retry or finish instead of staying active.
  • Return task status to LLM when changing. #556

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.150.1
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Add Claude Opus 5 support.
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html: • Add Claude Opus 5 support.

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.150.0
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Abort in-flight LLM streaming requests promptly on prompt stop for OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, Google, Ollama and custom OpenAI-compatible providers (previously only Anthropic/Bedrock), including while waiting for the first token. #554 Don't reset a chat's model…
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html:
• Abort in-flight LLM streaming requests promptly on prompt stop for OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, Google, Ollama and custom OpenAI-compatible providers (previously only Anthropic/Bedrock), including while waiting for the first token. #554

  • Don't reset a chat's model when changing the agent of an already started chat; the agent's defaultModel now only applies to chats without an established model. editor-code-assistant/eca-emacs#282

  • Fix plugin-provided agents missing from the editor's agent list when model sync finishes before plugin resolution (common with providers using fetchModels: false): re-emit the chat config after plugins resolve.

  • Surface Anthropic refusal stop reason (e.g. Fable safety classifiers) as a clear chat message with Anthropic's category/explanation instead of silently ending the prompt.

  • Improve @/# completion performance: enumerate files via git ls-files instead of walking the whole tree, cache dir candidates and avoid re-computing sort keys.

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.149.1
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Add text chat context type: inline client-supplied text (e.g. editor buffers, terminal output) with a label and content, delivered with the user message like images. Allows clients to send content that has no filesystem path.
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html: • Add text chat context type: inline client-supplied text (e.g. editor buffers, terminal output) with a label and content, delivered with the user message like images. Allows clients to send content that has no filesystem path.

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.149.0
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Resolve plugin dependencies transitively: marketplace entries and .eca-plugin/plugin.json can declare plugins auto-loaded with the install. #552
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html: • Resolve plugin dependencies transitively: marketplace entries and .eca-plugin/plugin.json can declare plugins auto-loaded with the install. #552

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.148.2
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Recover when the provider rejects an image in the request (e.g. xAI's 512px minimum on MCP tool images): retry without images instead of failing every subsequent prompt.
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html: • Recover when the provider rejects an image in the request (e.g. xAI's 512px minimum on MCP tool images): retry without images instead of failing every subsequent prompt.

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.148.1
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Fix OpenRouter models failing every prompt with a context-window error: ignore catalog output limits >= context window and use limits from the provider's /models endpoint. Extend deepseek-v4 thinking variants (none, high, max) to also match deepseek-v4-flash…
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html:
• Fix OpenRouter models failing every prompt with a context-window error: ignore catalog output limits >= context window and use limits from the provider's /models endpoint.
  • Extend deepseek-v4 thinking variants (none, high, max) to also match deepseek-v4-flash models.
  • Fix duplicate errors when a dead connection fails several stacked requests at once, which broke the auto-continue recovery and leaked state into the next prompt. #547

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.148.0
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Improve resilience to connections dropped by proxies/networks: retry stale pooled connections, classify the error clearly, auto-continue up to 3 times per prompt. #547 Fix streaming tool calls dropped when provider sends empty-string id in subsequent chunks…
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html:
• Improve resilience to connections dropped by proxies/networks: retry stale pooled connections, classify the error clearly, auto-continue up to 3 times per prompt. #547
  • Fix streaming tool calls dropped when provider sends empty-string id in subsequent chunks (e.g. DashScope/Qwen Cloud).
  • Truncate oversized failed tool output, preserving full logs on disk instead of overflowing the model context.
  • Honor model output limits in OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Ollama requests while preserving extraPayload overrides.
  • Respect maxSteps in Markdown agent definitions.
  • Support variant in Markdown agent frontmatter.

gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.title: ECA 0.147.3
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.summary: Fix remote server silently falling back to HTTP when the TLS private key is in SEC1 EC format; validate keys before caching and log HTTP fallback. #521
gh-editor-code-assistant-eca.html: • Fix remote server silently falling back to HTTP when the TLS private key is in SEC1 EC format; validate keys before caching and log HTTP fallback. #521

gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.title: Mistral Vibe v3.0.1
gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.summary: Added New enable_auto_approve setting: when the admin-managed config sets it to false, the auto-approve (YOLO) mode is forbidden — the auto-approve agent (and any custom agent with safety = "yolo") is hidden and --auto-approve/--yolo plus…
gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.html:
Added
  • New enable_auto_approve setting: when the admin-managed config sets it to false, the auto-approve (YOLO) mode is forbidden — the auto-approve agent (and any custom agent with safety = "yolo") is hidden and --auto-approve/--yolo plus bypass_tool_permissions are ignored. Per-tool permissions still apply.
  • compaction_max_output_tokens (80000), compaction_thinking (unset), compaction_reasoning_limit_tokens (32000), output_limit_retries (6) and output_token_reserve (4096) settings tune compaction requests and recovery from answers cut off at the output limit.
  • The app server has experimental session/subagents/wait, session/subagents/interrupt and session/subagents/read methods: a client can wait for the subagents a turn left running, interrupt them, and read each one's status, store, model, usage, cost and steps
  • vibe -p waits for the subagents its turn left running before it exits; --time-limit and other stops interrupt them, and the --output-dir export lists each subagent with its status, model, usage, cost and steps, and copies its journal
  • Each subagent's cost is priced at its own model's rates; when its model is unknown, the root's rates price it and the row says so (pricingModel, pricingFallback)
  • An --agent-socket server's tools/call names its caller, so the server can tell a subagent's call from the root's
  • A custom tool that fails to load now shows a warning naming the file and the error, instead of disappearing silently.
  • Experimental vibe run-server command: runs many vibe -p --agent-socket sessions from one process, on shared app-servers (--runs-per-app-server, default 16) that exit once idle, each run with its own config, credentials, limits and export
  • Vibe Desktop sessions support scheduled loops: the assistant can schedule a recurring prompt, fired prompts show as loop cards in the conversation, and active loops are listed (and can be deleted) in the session info.
Changed
  • /model and the /config model list now group models by where they come from: your organization, experiments, the model catalog, then your own config.
  • Resuming or continuing a session keeps the agent it last ran on, even if your default agent changes; switch agents in the session to change it.
  • ACP usage updates now report the session's prompt-cache hits as cached read tokens.
  • A tool output past about 16,000 characters is saved to a file, and the model sees its start and end instead of only its start.
  • A bash command that times out returns what it printed, and the default timeout is now 120 seconds, up to 300 when asked.
  • tools.bash.default_timeout and max_timeout_seconds are unset unless set in config.toml; the native shell tools still default to 300 seconds, at most 600 or the default when that is longer.
  • A shell tool's default_timeout above its max_timeout_seconds is now a config error naming both, instead of being lowered to the maximum.
  • read_file reports the file's line count and where to read on, and an offset past the end is an error.
  • read_file on a directory lists its entries, up to 500 at a time, instead of failing.
  • read_file and file mentions return up to 64,000 bytes a call instead of 51,200, the same as the Agents SDK.
  • On Linux, a command that runs the machine out of memory is the first process the kernel stops, before Vibe itself.
  • A shell's login profile runs before a session's first command and outside its timeout, and one that fails or takes over 10 seconds is skipped with a warning.
  • Bash commands can call the functions and aliases the login profile defines, for bash and zsh, and a change to a profile file is picked up by the next command.
  • Vibe now supports Python 3.12 and later instead of requiring Python 3.14.
  • All Vibe skill descriptions now support up to 1,024 characters.
Fixed
  • Background process results from the app server keep their process ID and exit code.
  • A model response kept open by keepalives without sending any data now times out after api_timeout instead of hanging the session.
  • An unparseable VIBE_* environment variable such as VIBE_MODELS is now ignored and logged instead of stopping Vibe at startup.
  • Sessions now record the agent they run on, so a session started with --agent reopens on that agent.
  • Code the agent runs with run_typescript now sees an MCP or connector tool's own error text instead of a generic message.
  • A failed /clear keeps the conversation on screen, and failed /clear and rewind requests show the server's reason.
  • Picking a model your administrator enforces explains why the model does not change.
  • Resuming a session from the picker restores its queued prompts.
  • A malformed background-process call now fails that tool call instead of ending the session.
  • When you have not chosen a model, a new session's first message now waits up to 5 seconds for the model assigned to your account.
  • Editors that sign in on every connection over ACP, such as CodeCompanion.nvim, no longer open a browser sign-in page when Vibe already has an API key for that console.
  • With enable_system_trust_store = true in config.toml, prompts now also use the operating system's certificates, so they work behind corporate proxies that only the OS trusts.
  • Turns no longer fail when the model announces a tool call but sends none, or sends one without a name; Vibe retries once or ends the turn cleanly instead.
  • The welcome banner text no longer shifts when you switch to or from a Mistral Large model.
  • Connectors that need no login, such as DeepWiki, now show as not connected in /mcp instead of error - try refreshing, and pressing Enter connects them without visiting the dashboard.
  • The CLI no longer hangs when it talks to an app-server that has already exited, such as after cancelling setup during a slow startup
  • Hovering a subagent row with the ansi-dark theme no longer turns its text black on black
  • Clicking a hovered subagent row no longer flashes the highlight back to the previous row
  • Installs and launches through uv now force a GIL-enabled build of Python, fixing failures on machines with a free-threaded (no-GIL) Python 3.14 installed.
  • Compaction no longer fails when a provider's cache repeats a malformed summary, or spends its whole output budget reasoning; Vibe falls back to a simpler request instead.
  • An answer cut off at the output-token limit no longer ends the turn at once: it is discarded and asked for again with feedback, up to 6 times a turn.
  • A tool call cut off at the output-token limit, such as a large file write, is asked for again in smaller pieces instead of failing with a JSON error.
  • Tool argument errors now name the field at fault, the allowed fields and the one the model most likely meant.
  • A failed edit now shows the closest matching text in the file, or the lines where a repeated match occurs.
  • Requests to a model with a declared max_context_length no longer overflow its window: the output cap is clipped to the room the input leaves, less a 4096-token reserve.
  • Bash commands no longer lose PATH entries that a login profile resets, and the profile runs once per session.
  • Bash commands still run after a command deleted /dev/null.
  • The git context names the repository's default branch instead of always main, and no longer hedges the instructions a session starts with.
  • In a sandbox, the git context is read in one round trip, and no longer times out on a slow sandbox.
  • Cached input tokens now reach the session's token usage and runtime stats, so vibe -p reports and prices them
  • Plugins that set a displayName in their ai.mistral.vibe extension now load their knowledge, hooks, agents and tool namespace instead of reporting an extension error.
  • vibe -p exits only once its app-server has, and on Linux a killed vibe -p or vibe run-server takes its app-servers down with it

gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.title: Mistral Vibe v3.0.0
gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.summary: Added The app-server reports each model's compaction threshold, so a client can show how full a session's context is before it compacts. Desktop can import projects and sessions from another coding agent during onboarding. Rust CLI: /leanstall and /unleanstall…
gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.html:
Added
  • The app-server reports each model's compaction threshold, so a client can show how full a session's context is before it compacts.
  • Desktop can import projects and sessions from another coding agent during onboarding.
  • Rust CLI: /leanstall and /unleanstall install and uninstall the Lean agent.
  • With experimental_enable_model_catalog on, the model list includes Mistral's curated models, and your config can still override their settings.
  • Rust CLI: Tool approval options, /thinking levels, /resume sessions and /log-level rows and badges can be clicked.
  • Rust CLI: Option lists show a faint hover background under the mouse.
  • With a "shared only" API key, /mcp blocks connectors that need your login and tells you to run vibe --setup.
  • Rust CLI: /branch forks the current conversation into a new resumable session.
  • The agent can now wait for your next message or for background work to finish, instead of repeatedly checking.
  • Rust CLI: Debug console for live session logs, opened with /debug or Ctrl+.
  • Rust CLI: Report activity, approvals, questions, completion, and failure with session titles and error messages through the OSC 7501 Program Status Protocol.
  • /status shows the credential source in use and the shadowed sources
  • Admin-enforceable enable_mcp flag to block all user-facing MCP server operations (add, remove, toggle, login, logout, tool registration), including plugin-provided MCP servers, via managed config.
Changed
  • read_file shows a file's line endings as they are on disk, like shell commands do
  • write_file writes new files with the line endings it is given, also on Windows
  • The app server now shows up as vibe-app-server instead of python3 in Activity Monitor, ps, and top.
  • Rust CLI: dragging a scrollbar moves smoothly in fine steps on terminals that report the mouse in pixels, such as Ghostty, kitty and WezTerm.
  • displayed_workdir, context_warnings and raise_on_compaction_failure are deprecated: they remain accepted in existing configs but have no effect on Unified execution.
  • Rust CLI: The welcome banner starts at the top left, with the conversation and what's new flowing below it while queued messages stay at the bottom.
  • Rust CLI: One click picks an option whose only action is choosing it (tool approvals, questions, /theme, /plugins, subagents, config choices, the remote project picker, MCP or connector sign-in); options with several actions (/model, /thinking, /resume, /mcp, /config) highlight on the first click and confirm on the second.
  • Rust CLI: The highlighted free-text answer spans the full row, and clicking its number unticks it in multi-select questions.
  • Rust CLI: Colored text on a highlighted row takes the row's text color.
  • Rust CLI: headless mode (-p) now follows the Python CLI's run contract, with turn, token, price and time limits, graceful stops, and a JSON run export whose exit code reports the outcome.
  • Pressing Esc twice to clear the input or open rewind now accepts a slower second press.
  • Rust CLI: The welcome banner is more compact: the cat sits beside the version, model and plan, and the model, connector, MCP server, skill and hook counts are gone.
  • The Vibe VS Code extension (ACP surface) now gets the same background session titles as CLI and Desktop; the sessions list shows the summarized title instead of the message preview
  • The agent's subagent tools are renamed from subagent.* to agents.*, and sessions saved with the old names still resume.
  • Plugins can no longer use the agents, agent or collaboration tool namespaces, which are reserved for built-in agent tools.
  • A programmatic tool call now stops after 60 seconds in total, and a single sleep inside it is capped at 30 seconds.
  • Faster session startup when no MCP server is used.
  • Vibe now requires Python 3.14 or newer (previously 3.12)
  • Outbound HTTPS connections now validate certificate chains with stricter RFC 5280 rules; a private CA missing SKID/AKID or KeyUsage extensions may be rejected — set enable_system_trust_store or use a compliant CA
  • Vibe Code: the retry notice keeps counting the seconds past the planned retry instead of freezing until the provider answers, and screen readers get paced progress announcements
  • vibe -p JSON and streaming output mark each completed assistant message and reasoning with an outcome: committed, or discarded with its cause.
  • The Rust TUI detects terminal activity reporting support to avoid duplicate title indicators and notification bells.
  • Faster session startup, most noticeably on Windows and in repositories with many branches or tags.
Fixed
  • Desktop local Code holds queued messages while editing without a timeout; Save and Cancel let the queue continue unless paused.
  • Disconnecting during an unfinished queued edit keeps the original message and pauses the queue until Resume.
  • In Vibe Desktop, the sidebar session list now only reorders when a new conversation turn starts, instead of jumping around on queued messages, steers, and permission answers.
  • On Windows, the shell tools no longer auto-approve commands that use a mid-word #, an escaped quote, or PowerShell quoting to hide part of the command from the approval check.
  • Multi-line edits to CRLF files no longer fail, and edited lines keep the file's line endings
  • The Unified Harness no longer converts a CRLF file to LF when it overwrites it
  • Sessions containing a large image no longer fail with a compaction error when the context is nowhere near full.
  • Listing saved sessions (/resume and the Desktop session sidebar) is several times faster when you have thousands of sessions.
  • Rust CLI: scrolling with the wheel or a scrollbar no longer stutters or trails the pointer when the view is slow to redraw.
  • Rust CLI: the smart approve mode now shows its warning-colored input border and cycles with Shift+Tab, matching the Python CLI.
  • Automatic context compaction now shows a progress row in the transcript that settles to done, failed, or interrupted.
  • The current input line no longer blinks with the cursor in the textual-dark theme.
  • A suspended Rust CLI now dies when its terminal closes or it is killed, instead of lingering forever.
  • Resuming a suspended session with shell bg twice no longer exits the CLI with an interrupted-syscall error.
  • Rust CLI: Fix shell MCP commands to support named URLs, static authentication, stdio servers, and timeout options.
  • Rust CLI: /mcp add, login, logout, and status errors now show the server's reason.
  • Session meta.json records the active model and provider model name for Unified Harness sessions.
  • Subagents now see connector tools in sessions whose connector catalog finishes loading after the session starts, and connector changes applied mid-session reach subagents spawned afterwards.
  • Starting, resuming, or continuing another session no longer resets the shared host's resolved connector catalog to its start-time placeholder, so a session promoted after that keeps its connector grants.
  • Rust CLI: config validation warnings that appear mid-session now surface as a toast, not only at startup.
  • Very large tool outputs are truncated in the transcript, so sessions containing them can be previewed and resumed again.
  • Rust CLI: A session preview that fails to load no longer closes the resume picker or makes the CLI unusable.
  • Rust CLI: The /rename usage tip and /mcp add --help show their <...> placeholders instead of dropping them.
  • A locked or unapproved macOS Keychain no longer hangs vibe -p forever: the read gives up after 60s and the error says the Keychain could not be read instead of reporting a missing key.
  • Rust CLI: -p runs announce on stderr when the API key comes from the keyring, fail if startup stalls, and print the server's error instead of a bare session/start.
  • When a third-party model declines a request, Vibe now says so instead of recording an empty reply.
  • Sessions where a third-party model returned an empty reply no longer fail every later message with a 400 error.

gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.title: Mistral Vibe v2.26.1
gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.summary: Added The app-server reports which process holds a stored session, and pushes a change when that process lets go of it, so a client can show a session open elsewhere as read-only Rust CLI: Configure proxy and SSL certificate settings with /proxy-setup. Rust…
gh-mistralai-mistral-vibe.html:
Added
  • The app-server reports which process holds a stored session, and pushes a change when that process lets go of it, so a client can show a session open elsewhere as read-only
  • Rust CLI: Configure proxy and SSL certificate settings with /proxy-setup.
  • Rust CLI: The narrator reads each turn's summary aloud and shows a speaking status row that Esc or Ctrl+C stops.
  • Rust CLI: /plugins browses the session's plugins, and /reload-plugins re-pins them and reports what changed.
  • Rust CLI: Free-text answers to agent questions accept multiple lines, multi-line pastes, and click-to-place caret.
  • Rust CLI: In the /model and /thinking pickers, s applies the selection for the current session only, while Enter still saves it to your config.
  • Rust CLI: Picking a model immediately opens the thinking level picker for that model, and both are applied together (Esc cancels both); after a session-only model pick, the thinking level is session-only too.
  • nix run .#rustCli to launch the Rust terminal instead of the Python one
  • Rust CLI: /whoami shows the start of your API key, its scope, and its access scope.
  • Space toggles the focused checkbox in multi-select questions.
  • enable_background_processes = false stops the agent from starting background processes
  • enable_subagents = false takes subagents away from the agent on the default runtime.
  • Disable main input cursor blinking with cursor_blink = false or /config, keeping a steady caret in both Python and Rust terminals.
  • Document Library connector: search, list, open, and fetch documents from your Mistral document libraries directly in Vibe.
  • export.json records steps, the number of model calls the agent made
  • export.json lists the session's config issues, such as a skill it could not load, under warnings
  • vibe -p reads the prompt from --prompt-file or stdin, and --output-dir writes an export.json and the session journal on every exit.
  • vibe -p --time-limit SECONDS stops the run at a deadline; SIGTERM and Ctrl-C stop it the same way, and the session can be resumed.
  • Per-model top_p and max_output_tokens config settings.
  • Experimental experimental_enable_model_catalog config flag (default off) — groundwork for the upcoming model catalog, no visible effect yet.
  • New api_stream_idle_timeout setting (off by default) fails a model response that goes silent for that many seconds.
  • vibe -p --agent-socket sessions run background processes in their POSIX sandbox, as enable_background_processes says, instead of always turning them off
  • New title_prompt_id config setting to override the prompt used to generate session titles: built-in session_title or a custom .md file from ~/.vibe/prompts/ or .vibe/prompts/.
Changed
  • New sessions start their first turn faster, and long sessions open, load older messages and resume sooner.
  • /status shows token counts in a compact form (e.g. 1.23M) followed by the exact value, dimmed, with thousands separators.
  • The context usage indicator and subagent token counts round to three significant digits (e.g. 12.5k instead of 12k).
  • Rust CLI: Queue selection removes the highlighted prompt with Backspace or Ctrl+C instead of Backspace or Delete.
  • Rust CLI: Tool group headers count each kind of call (e.g. "Read 10 files, ran 3 commands"), a single visible entry is no longer folded into a group, and result borders line up under their toggle arrows, wrapped headers included.
  • The off thinking level now actually disables reasoning on models whose offered levels include it, instead of silently leaving the server's default in charge.
  • The default model's thinking levels are now off and high; a stored low pick resets to off and a stored medium pick resets to high.
  • The default model declares a 256k context window; auto-compaction now derives from it.
  • A stale pin to the removed local model now warns and falls back to the hosted default.
  • Rust CLI: In text inputs, Cmd+Left/Right, Home/End and Ctrl+A/E at a line edge move on to the previous line start or the next line end.
  • Rust CLI: Shortcut hints use the same wording everywhere, and j/k navigate every list.
  • Rust CLI: /config, /mcp, /plugins and the project picker search with /; Esc leaves the search, then clears it, then closes. /plugins now shows its search field under the title, like /mcp and /config.
  • Rust CLI: Every list marks the focused row with the same highlight bar, and a green › marks the current value.
  • Rust CLI: Lists wrap at both ends and scroll back to their very top, Esc always goes back one level, and numbered options take their digit.
  • Your Mistral identity and plan now show in /whoami and the banner even when the active model isn't a Mistral model.
  • Rust CLI: Typing /, ! or & over a fully selected input switches to that mode, and so does pasting a /command or !command into an empty input.
  • Rust CLI: the startup banner hint now reads "You are using the new Vibe TUI. To switch back to the classic TUI, set the VIBE_CLI environment variable to python."
  • Stopping a background process now also stops what it started in the background, and returns only once all of it has exited
  • A background process now keeps running until everything it started in the background has exited, not just its shell
  • The Document Library connector is now gated behind the experimental_enable_document_library_connector config flag (off by default) while its tools stabilize.
  • vibe -p exits 1 on usage or config errors, 2 on infrastructure failures and 3 when a limit or a model refusal stopped the agent
  • vibe -p --max-turns now exits 3, not 1, when the agent reaches the turn limit; so do --max-tokens and --max-price, including when the budget ran out as the agent finished
  • Model requests retry HTTP 520.
  • Rust CLI: The welcome banner starts at the top left, with the conversation and what's new flowing below it while queued messages stay at the bottom.
Fixed
  • Browser sign-in now explains when your workspace can't be used and asks you to select another one, instead of showing a generic error.
  • Rust CLI: Ctrl+G opens the current input in $VISUAL / $EDITOR and loads the saved text back.
  • Rust CLI: A chat input selection no longer reappears after an approval, a question, or the subagent list takes focus.
  • Rust CLI: Text stays selectable and copyable while an approval, question, picker, or other bottom panel is open, including the transcript, the loading row, and the panel itself.
  • /reload-plugins now offers the skills of a plugin installed during the session, without a restart.
  • Rust CLI: Copying a selection no longer adds line breaks or indentation where long text wraps on screen.
  • Rust CLI: Copying wide characters such as CJK text no longer inserts a space after each one.
  • Rust CLI: Selecting or copying a wrapped or multi-line transcript row no longer picks up its hang indent.
  • Rust CLI: Long lines in an expanded thought now wrap inside its border and indent.
  • Rust CLI: Queue selection and edit controls replace the loading hints for as long as the mode lasts, instead of a notice that timed out or lingered.
  • Rust CLI: The loading hints no longer offer steering or queued-message cancellation when Enter or Ctrl+C would do something else.
  • Rust CLI: Long free-text answers to agent questions wrap instead of overflowing the question box.
  • Rust CLI: Answered questions show a check mark instead of an expand arrow that did nothing.
  • A corrupted MCP OAuth token in the keychain no longer crashes Vibe; the server just asks you to log in again
  • Tool calls with a very large result (e.g. reading a big file) keep their tool-specific header, marked as truncated, instead of showing as a generic tool call.
