gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
Oh My Hermes 4.0.1 — graph master

graph master is the graph-engineering release. A big job can now run on its own as a graph of delegated nodes, the work Hermes hands out is drawn as a graph you can open and steer, and the routes that start paid runs got stricter about when they start one.

dag-ulw: a big job runs as a graph

Say dag ulw <goal> (also ulw dag, /dag-ulw, dag ulw해줘), or ask for a big job whose words say how it splits or how wide it reaches. Hermes plans it as a graph of small nodes, runs the ready ones in parallel on its own delegate_task children, settles each from its handoff file, verifies the goal with a separate node, repairs failed nodes (two cycles each), and adds the work the goal check finds missing to the same run (two rounds) before it reports. It asks only for scope, spend or an irreversible step. (#2185)

dag-ulw also works on a Docker or SSH terminal whose user has a writable home: each node writes its handoff under the terminal user's own home, read once through Hermes' live environment, so a remote run no longer fails every node with handoff_missing. (#2205) Each delegated goal ends with its run marker, so a preview shows the task. (#2203)

The delegation graph you can see

Delegated work (delegate_task children, omh_team parts, fanout units) is drawn as a graph in the OMH TUI and in omh hud --graph, and chat replies get the run's start, its count changes and its end, never the boxes. (#2179) The boxes stand in frontiers with state colours, Dependencies lists every recorded edge exactly, and /dag opens an interactive full-screen view. (#2191, #2199) The graph survives Hermes' rotating compaction (#2201), and each lane carries its subagent's output tokens, as does the agent view that now sits under the composer. (#2188, #2192, #2194, #2200)

Routing safety: a stop or a question never starts a paid run

A complaint, a question or a stop that opens with a skill's name (ultrawork broke my build, dag ulw는 뭐야?, ultrawork stop, loop 멈춰) is answered directly; neither the router nor Hermes' route hint runs the skill. (#2207) dag-ulw routing reads remarks, bug reports and questions as such, and a polite request as a run. (#2197) A delegation route is refused when Hermes would send the child somewhere other than where the route says (#2180, #2202), and fallback advances only the calling conversation's own route. (#2177)

Restarts and compaction hand work back

A Hermes restart no longer leaves an omh_team part waiting four hours: the first team_start after a restart hands back each part whose process is gone, same attempt, no try spent. (#2198) A Hermes compaction no longer reads as the end of the work for the delegation route or omh_team. (#2176)

Read-only Hermes stores through a quoted URI

A Hermes home whose path holds #, ?, or a % followed by two hex digits is read, and no stray file is created beside it: every read-only open of state.db and kanban.db goes through one helper that quotes the path. (#2209)

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
Oh My Hermes 4.0.0 — Zeus ⚡

Zeus brings three major changes to OMH: a dedicated terminal, long-term memory you can maintain through conversation, and specialist workflows connected to Hermes’ native capabilities.

🖥️ A dedicated OMH terminal

Work with Hermes through OMH’s own terminal interface. Follow tool calls, inspect diffs, check subagents, and steer a running task without leaving the conversation. Session pickers, history search, rewind, and clearer approval and question controls make longer sessions easier to navigate.

Run omh for the OMH terminal or hermes for the stock Hermes interface. OMH’s plugin capabilities remain available in Hermes.

🧠 Long-term memory, maintained through conversation

Search, confirm, correct, and retire memories by talking to your agent. When Hermes’ built-in memory fills up, OMH can preserve approved copies in its long-term store before freeing native memory space.

Retrieval prioritizes relevant context and current values. Memory support extends across TUI, Desktop, and supported messenger conversations, with user, channel, project, and profile boundaries governing what can be recalled.

🔗 Specialist workflows, connected to native Hermes

Bring domain-specific methods into research, planning, coding, design, and everyday work without maintaining a second set of controls.

OMH workflows now use more of Hermes’ native capabilities: one plan checklist, source registration and citation checks, structured review results, Automation Blueprints, and recorded outputs from document and image tools.

More powerful ULW workflows

Set up subagent model routing with /omh-model in the OMH terminal. Choose the model and reasoning effort for each task category, then use ULW to research, plan, and run independent work in parallel.

Upgrade

omh update

Restart or reload Hermes after updating. Launch with omh.

The OMH terminal falls back to Hermes’ own interface on unsupported environments, including Windows. Updates release OMH-owned styling from the stock Hermes interface while preserving user-owned customizations.

The complete version-bound changelog follows below.

Full changelog

  • Indonesian ships as a trigger language pack. src/routing/trigger_packs/id.json, contributed by @fauzibrevy-hub (#2154), covers the 21 skills the ja and zh packs cover, with phrases such as tinjau kode, audit aksesibilitas, build gagal and lakukan riset mendalam. It is the first pack in a Latin-script language, and that shares the English token space: Indonesian borrows bug, crash, error and file. So a shipped pack phrase written entirely in ASCII now scores only as a whole phrase. Its words never join the skill's trigger tokens, and the lexical shortlist leaves it out of the skill's English document and anchors. Tests hold every skill's trigger tokens, lexical document and anchors equal to the view with its ASCII pack phrases taken out, and refuse an ASCII hold-back entry that none of the pack's own non-ASCII phrases carries. ASCII pack phrases merge after the ja, ko and zh ones, so SKILL.md descriptions and capability rows, which show only a skill's first triggers, keep the cues they showed before. Phrases that routed ordinary Indonesian chat (a team work plan, "ask me one at a time", a medicine reminder) did not ship, and neither did a few that read as word-for-word translations. ultrawork carries one Indonesian phrase, implementasi paralel: its always-loaded body had room for one under the byte ceiling. id is an input language only: it is not a --language / OMH_LANG output choice.

  • OMH TUI tool calls read as in Claude Code. Each call is one row, ⏺ read_file(README.md) 0.2s: a ⏺ in the accent while it runs, green once done, red when it failed or was denied, in place of the ✓ and ✗ marks, then the tool's name and what it ran on in parentheses. What it printed, and an edit's diff, hang under ⎿ , as a command's output does. A read or a load no longer echoes the first lines it read: it says Read 715 lines (read_file), loaded skill omh-docs (skill_view) or 12 matches (search_files). A resumed session's earlier calls read the same way, with a dim ⏺ (Hermes' record keeps no outcome) and an edit's diff under it, in place of the · read_file README.md rows with a blank row between each.

  • An answer you gave Hermes reads under the call it was about. The record of an approval or a question (✓ allowed once · <command>, ✓ blue · Which colour?) was written above the turn's live tool calls, so with one row per call it stood over the first read of the turn. It is now the first row under the call that asked, ⎿ ✓ allowed once · <command>, on the same green or red band; a denial reads ⏺ terminal(…), then ⎿ ✗ denied · …, then Hermes' denial line. With no call running (a subagent's question after its turn), it is still a row of its own. A clarify question Hermes timed out, or one you cancelled, says so once under its call (⎿ ✗ timed out · Which colour?), not again in a bare ⎿ timed out row under that.

  • An OMH TUI diff no longer doubles each changed line. Hermes pads every added and removed line of an edit's diff with spaces, to 143 columns in a live patch, so on any narrower terminal each green or red band wrapped into a second, empty band row. A diff line's trailing spaces are dropped now; the band still reaches the right edge.

  • The OMH TUI's working row reads as Claude Code's. It was a braille spinner and Hermes' kaomoji text (⠋ (⌐■_■) analyzing... (12s)). It is now ✶ Analyzing… (12s · ↓1.2k tokens · thinking with high effort · esc to interrupt): a glyph turning through · ✢ ✳ ✶ ✻ ✽ (still under reduced motion), Hermes' verb without its face or dots (Working… when it gives none; a stall or retry notice, No response from provider in 120s — reconnecting…, keeps its words), and the effort when the session reports one. A tip naming a key sits under it, one a turn, on a terminal 16 rows tall or more (⎿ Tip: ctrl+o shows the whole transcript); it is local text and nothing is sent. interrupting… lines up under the same glyph column.

  • Your prompt and a turn's end read as in Claude Code. A prompt in the OMH TUI transcript is a dim > and dim text, with no tinted band behind it, and a command's echo takes the same > (> /model). The ↳ you: … reminder over a running turn loses its band too: ↳ you: in the accent, your words dim. A turn's done line is one dim line under the reply, ✻ 5s · 3 tools · ↓1.3k, without the rule that ran to the right edge.

  • The OMH TUI's composer is a rounded box over one dim info line, as in Claude Code. The composer's two rules, the mode row and the dark status band are gone. The composer sits in a box (╭─╮, │ > … │, ╰─╯) that keeps its colour in every mode, and the line under it, two cells in under the box's text, says the mode or the keys that matter now on the left (? for shortcuts while the composer is empty, ⏵⏵ accept all on (⇧⇥ to cycle) in accept's colour, ⏸ plan mode on (⇧⇥ to cycle) in plan's, a question's or a picker's keys) and the model, ctx 5% and effort medium on the right, with the OMH HUD's repeat and in-flight tool counts first when there are any. The ⚚ OMH brand and the idle / running words are gone: the working row, the strip and the queue rows already say them, and during a turn the left names only the steer keys, since the working row already offers esc to interrupt. On a narrow terminal the right side gives way first, the model shortening to deepseek-v4.1-flash and then v4.1-flash before it goes. The line is on every terminal of 3 rows or more, so the mode is never hidden, and the agent list now opens from 6 rows (and 20 columns) instead of 10. A ! shell line keeps its ! shell

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
oh-my-hermes 3.0.2 · stable

Everything merged since 3.0.1 (2026-10-07), 33 pull requests. Per-entry detail is in the 3.0.2 section of CHANGELOG.md.

Why this release

Two themes. Skills now hold a stricter line on how work is planned, debugged, tested and approved (SkillEx), and parallel coding agents can no longer run, reach the network, or leave settings behind outside their fence (FenceGuard). Memory capture also stops admitting instructions disguised as facts.

Highlights

  • SkillEx: skills that work more carefully. (#2052–#2056, #2060–#2065, #2072)
    • A workflow name inside a block quote, a relayed line or a link no longer starts that workflow, and a delegated child is not told to start an orchestrating engine its brief names.
    • plan lists up to 5 inputs or failure modes no planned test covers; ralplan plans for the target state of whoever consumes the change and counts acceptance only from the user's answer.
    • app-debugging stops after three failed fixes on the same reproduction and re-examines the architecture.
    • loop reviews its design before launch: a finish line a program can decide, and a fence of paths checked against the diff.
    • ulw-work asks what a new test guards before it counts, settles small reversible questions as recorded Rulings, and caps review rounds.
    • deep-interview: a yes to an idea approves only the idea.
    • agent-debug reads past sessions read-only with every read length-capped; backend names one authoritative contract per service boundary.
  • FenceGuard: fanout stays in its fence.
    • Fanout no longer runs a unit unfenced without being told to. (#2026)
    • Git the dispatcher runs inside a fence gets no credentials and no network; host git no longer runs a unit's planted core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or filter driver. (#2034, #2039)
    • Diagnostics analyzers run fenced to their snapshot; the workspace preflight writes nothing into the unit's git directory, and a preflight the fenced tree failed is no longer reported as a host failure. (#2038, #2044, #2046)
    • A pre-spawn refusal no longer exits 0; Codex starts inside the macOS fence. (#2033, #2025)
  • Memory.
    • A model capture phrased as an order to its reader (you must…, Korean request endings) is refused with a next_action to restate it as an observation — no review step. (#2064)
    • Spelled-out, vague and past-relative time ("two weeks ago", "last Monday", "il y a une semaine") routes a capture to review. (#2043, #2051, #2059)
    • Recall reads French: accented Latin letters no longer split a word. (#2028)
    • A default-store install names ~/.omh for the plugin, so multiplexed processes load it. (#2047)
  • Also. Concurrent TUIs share one fanout scan and an idle widget polls less (#2066); model setup binds aliases on Hermes custom-provider machines (#2023); omh quality-evidence file-activity fails closed on symlink escapes (#2032); omh_agent_board survives Hermes dropping the bundle's modules (#2024).

Updating from 3.0.1

Run omh update, then restart any running Hermes session (TUI, Desktop, gateway). omh doctor confirms the active generation.

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes/main/install.ps1 | iex           # Windows
omh setup

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
oh-my-hermes 3.0.1 · stable

Everything merged since 3.0.0 (2026-09-29), 56 pull requests. Per-entry detail is in the 3.0.1 section of CHANGELOG.md.

Why this release

Long-term memory was being written but never read back: the turn-start hook order left every prefetch empty. 3.0.1 fixes that and removes the human approval step from the memory loop, then takes the opportunity to give several things that were copied by hand a single owner — and fixes the two defects that work uncovered.

Highlights

  • Long-term memory that works without an operator.
    • The memory provider renders its pack in the order Hermes calls its hooks, so recall reaches the model again. (#2001)
    • The model records memories itself through omh_memory capture; safe content is approved automatically, review-first stays available as a policy. (#2001, #2002)
    • Admission (capture, duplicate check, auto-safe approval, durability receipt) lives in the plugin bundle and the tool calls it in-process — no more locating an installed omh executable. (#2012)
    • omh memory pack scopes records the way recall does: explicit thread and project-identity packs are populated, a thread record travels only with its own session, and a pack for the resolved identity is the default pack under its own name, conflicts included. (#2016, #2019)
    • The bundle's store lock retries Windows permission denials with the one backoff definition the stores already used. (#2017)
  • One owner instead of hand-kept copies (no behaviour change). The router's prepared query, the run-record file names and schema versions, the per-turn budget ledger, the per-skill record, the executor-name phrase groups, the portable overrides and the per-turn text budgets each have a single definition that everything else reads. (#2003–#2011)
  • Import order can no longer change routing. The plugin bundle's standalone fallbacks bound themselves whenever the router was still mid-import, so /loop … was classified differently depending on which module a process loaded first. The guards and classifiers resolve per call, and the cycle itself (skills/__init__ loading the renderer eagerly) is gone. (#2013, #2015)
  • Every shipped skill installs under the Hermes install scanner. hermes skills install refused omh-routing and six other skills on wording alone (setgid, a > .claude/settings shape, "do not tell the user", a cryptocurrency name, sudo). The sentences are reworded at the source, and CI now runs the Hermes scanner itself over every shipped skill. (#2014, #2018, #2000)
  • Fanout units stay inside their worktree: Git runs there, commits land on the unit's own branch, Git LFS repositories work, a busy unit exits 75, and one function assembles every unit prompt. Windows dispatch stays unconfined as a measured finding.
  • Models. GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Grok Build 0.1 are registered and measured; Bedrock Claude ids resolve to the claude family; named custom providers route through delegation; the codestral calibration has a live measurement.
  • Install and update. omh setup --omh-home X binds the plugin to X; omh update keeps full-only skills and takes back a bot profile's store setting once its .env names the key; install.ps1 works on Windows PowerShell 5.1; the plugin declares a Hermes floor, not a window.
  • Replies and diagnostics. The persona owns the voice (MODEL_OPTI.md records which models keep a non-English persona's language); the per-turn route hint names only installed skills; one-word English replies decline the route question; agent-debug produces a bounded, cited incident report.

Updating from 3.0.0

Run omh update, then restart any running Hermes session (TUI, Desktop, gateway). omh doctor confirms the active generation. Hermes skill tap: hermes skills tap add rlaope/oh-my-hermes then hermes skills install rlaope/oh-my-hermes/skills/omh-routing --yes — this now passes the install scan.

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
oh-my-hermes 3.0.0 · stable

Everything merged since 2.0.5 (2026-09-22), 98 pull requests. Per-entry detail is in the 3.0.0 section of CHANGELOG.md.

Why a major

OMH has changed what it does with work, not only how it routes it. Until 2.0.5, OMH prepared plans, handoffs and routes and then stepped back. In 3.0.0 it keeps going until the work is checked:

  • a todo item closes on a recorded result;
  • a failed fanout unit is repaired in place;
  • an accepted plan can run as a team of Hermes delegates, each task closing on its own check.

Hermes users will see the change in the reply as well.

Highlights

  • Work that finishes.
    • A todo item marked done without a recorded result (tool call, file write, PR, CI run or team check) stays done_unverified and keeps the loop going. (#1928)
    • A fanout unit that fails its checks is repaired in its own worktree. This repeats until the checks pass or the repair budget is spent (default 2, cap 3); a spent budget stops with the reason named. (#1929)
    • A unit's "done" is held to the tests its own changes reach. (#1876, #1866)
  • Teammates on Hermes' runtime. omh_team turns an accepted plan into a checked delegate team:
    • each task has an owner, its dependencies, and one verification command;
    • that command is shown in full when the plan is approved;
    • a task closes only when its check was observed passing;
    • a forged record runs nothing;
    • check commands are held to a refusal list for shell escapes and invisible characters. (#1931)
  • Replies in the host's voice.
    • OMH's record vocabulary (schema ids, "contract", "receipt", "lane") stays out of the reply.
    • Orchestration decisions each carry one plain sentence in the reply language: the team split, which specialist took a task, the goal and done criterion, and a blocked reason. (#1930, #1837, #1851, #1834)
    • omh quality-evidence reply-lint checks those rules against real Hermes sessions. (#1848)
  • Hermes Desktop.
    • The bundle ships a Desktop half: an OMH pane and a status item carrying the TUI widget's information. (#1856, #1864)
    • Work started on one Hermes surface is picked up on another. (#1878)
  • Routing and skills.
    • Dispatch happens only on strong evidence; otherwise Hermes gets a lexical shortlist of candidate skills. (#1879, #1880, #1886, #1891)
    • Everyday-sense phrases no longer reach a skill. (#1910)

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
oh-my-hermes 2.0.5 · stable

Everything merged since 2.0.3 (2026-09-12), 142 pull requests.

2.0.4 was tagged and never published. Its cut ran green and pushed the tag, then the publication step was refused by GitHub — HTTP 422 ... body is too long (maximum is 125000 characters) against a 228,212-byte release body — and every step after it was skipped, so nothing reached npm, Homebrew or a release page. The tag stands as a record; 2.0.5 carries all of its work. That is why this release is large: 133 of these pull requests are the 2.0.4 range, described in the 2.0.4 section of CHANGELOG.md (103 entries), and the nine below it are new.

Why this release

Most of the 2.0.4 range was reported by someone who could not get past it. An install on a machine whose python3 is 3.9.6 failed with a resolver message about a version bound, and the omh that failed to install was then not on the path to say so. A menu redraw threw away the arrow keys pressed during it, and a free-text prompt answered the escape bytes instead. omh uninstall reversed one of the seven config.yaml keys setup writes. A skill named with an ordinary English word claimed every sentence that happened to spell it. A model that had made the same tool call four times running was warned, and made it again.

The nine that follow are mostly the release pipeline itself, found by the 2.0.4 failure and by sweeping the surfaces it touched.

Since the 2.0.4 tag

  • A planning run asks before it starts editing. A plan stamped awaiting_acceptance that reaches a file-mutating tool raises the host's own approval prompt rather than a refusal the model can ignore. Escalation is bound to the session that owns the plan — a stamped record with no owner escalates for nobody, which a reviewer caught after the full suite had passed over it. (#1794)
  • A release body is bounded by what it is published to. The bound that existed was 262,144 bytes against a surface that accepts 125,000 characters, so it could never have caught the 2.0.4 overflow. An oversized section is now trimmed to whole entries plus a trailer naming what was left out and where; a section inside the bound is returned byte for byte. Counted in UTF-16 code units, the wider of the two readings of "characters". (#1798)
  • A cut asks for the site rebuild its own push cannot start. A cut pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub creates no workflow run from an event that token caused; Pages listens for a push touching site/**, which the version bump always rewrites. So the one push that changed the advertised version was the one push Pages never saw, and the public badge kept the previous version until an unrelated merge happened to touch a watched path. The cut now dispatches pages.yml, with continue-on-error so a failed rebuild cannot repaint a finished release as a failed one. (#1800)
  • Non-generative models are recognized and refused coding work by name, omh doctor reports which Jev-class plugins a machine holds, an undecidable route records the typed question it could not answer, and the routing corpora can be asked as typed questions anything can answer and scored. (#1804, #1806, #1811, #1812)
  • Tool identity is complete or it is unknown. Argument fingerprinting digests the whole argument set or marks the identity unknown rather than fingerprinting a prefix. (#1805, from an outside contributor)
  • The HUD route label drops a comparison its reader could not check. A lane routed to the model the parent session runs read category:deep(model =parent); the token compared the row's model against the parent's, which no row on that screen shows. The tokens that remain each name an event in the route. (#1797)

Highlights of the unpublished 2.0.4 range

  • Install works on the Python you have. The installer picks an interpreter the wheel can be installed into, names the ones it rejected and why, and provisions one when none qualifies; install.ps1 mirrors it, held by an environment-variable parity gate. (#1771, #1636)
  • The setup wizard stops fighting the keyboard. Menus keep keys pressed while redrawing and read a whole keypress instead of its first three bytes; control input typed into a free-text prompt is stripped rather than answered and echoed back; the wizard says where you are in its questions, and asks once whether OMH should watch for its own updates. (#1779, #1774, #1775, #1784, #1586)
  • Uninstall reverses what setup wrote — all seven config.yaml keys rather than one, under a single write discipline, with no emptied containers left behind. (#1764, #1765, #1770)
  • A repeated tool call is refused, then put to the person. The guard is cycle-aware and result-aware, an identical repeat is refused outright, an ignored refusal reaches a person, and the HUD shows repeat xN. (#1708, #1745, #1760)
  • Routing stops claiming sentences it does not own. A skill's own name no longer claims every sentence that spells it; three reported misroutes reach the skill that owns the question; ulw plan reaches the plan engine; saying a plan is fine no longer restarts it. (#1758, #1606, #1608, #1661, #1645, #1659, #1631, #1759, #1747)
  • The HUD tells one session's work from another's — each TUI's plan panel renders its own session, a delegate row gets its route and label back, and the HUD attests the model that answered against the model requested. (#1673, #1791, #1776, #1744, #1736, #1588)
  • A plan is a thing you can finish. A ten-phase code story ships as a stampable template; the deep guide, ELI5 pass, quiz, manual test guide and the close that ends a story each got an owner; a blocked item's recorded reason renders on the row. (#1780, #1781, #1785, #1787, #1660, #1686, #1616, #1647, #1549, #1705, #1751)
  • The plugin bundle survives its own failures — it loads without the omh package, and a session no profile owns is no longer vetoed out of every tool call. (#1669, #1677, #1762, #1763, #1761)
  • Long documents are planned before they are read — numbered read ranges, one frozen unit per range, a very large PDF read in page-anchored ranges, and a refused re-read that names the offset. (#1532, #1537, #1533, #1531, #1735, #1530)
  • Audit, fences and readiness. Declared hook semantics classified before you enable a plugin, plugin self-replacement paths named, fanout's write fence fixed on Linux, and three readiness checks — model data policy, plugin enforcement, profile isolation. (#1555, #1685, #1702, #1601, #1684, #1630, #1587)
  • Models and providers. A model-chain picker in the CLI and /omh-model in the Modern TUI, both editing the store a bot profile dispatches from; providers Hermes is linked to counted without an interview; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's override measured and revised. (#1506, #1507, #1680, #1519, #1524, #1628, #1526)

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
oh-my-hermes 2.0.3 · stable

Everything merged since 2.0.2 (2026-09-07), 75 pull requests. The grouped summary is in CHANGELOG.md; the full list is below.

Why this release

A dispatched unit could stop working and report nothing. A provider's session limit classified as crash; a batch whose every unit failed exited 0, so a caller reading the status was told the work succeeded; a worker alive for 36 minutes retrying one git workaround read as progress because its process existed; and a plan with open items sat unchanged while every turn ended on a status report. Each of those was a separate defect and together they made a stalled run indistinguishable from a working one. This release closes that chain, and adds the refusal that would have prevented the 36 minutes: a unit whose workspace cannot take the work never spawns.

Highlights

  • A failed dispatch stops reporting success. A provider's session limit classifies as limit-shaped, not a crash, and any unit carrying a failure_kind makes the command exit non-zero. A derived gate re-discovers every *_exit_code mapper from source and fails one that maps failed work to 0. (#1486, #1492)
  • Process alive and work progressing are different states, and never render the same. running requires new evidence; a live process without it is progress_stalled, beside awaiting_input, permission_blocked, account_limit, data_missing, failed, and verified — the only success state, which requires a validated result record, so exit 0 with no record is failed. Progress is read from the unit's own output, including the same failure line repeating while bytes still grow. The status board, plugin reader, TUI widget and omh coding fanout status --json all carry the state, its reason, and how long output has been still; the roster answers the poll loop's own question with all_units_terminal and stuck_units. (#1488, #1491)
  • The workspace is probed before the spawn, not after the failure. File write, git index write, the objects the work needs actually present (including a partial clone whose promisor fetch is forbidden), and case-only filename collisions on a case-insensitive filesystem — all in the unit's own isolation, with no network call. A failing check ends the unit as workspace_blocked before any CLI starts. Executor readiness stops claiming more than it saw: a passing --version is recorded as binary_version_only. (#1489)
  • Recovery matches the cause. A permission denial re-probes the workspace; a limit checks the account and its reset before any retry; missing objects are supplemented and verified before one unit resumes; a stall is re-run only with changed conditions or from a checkpoint. A live in-flight marker on a scope outranks every cause — no second worker is added to work already running. The account a CLI is configured with is recorded as a redacted one-way tag, so a limit can be told apart from the account that hit it. (#1497)
  • The plan drives the work. Open items mean the plan is not finished: the per-turn reminder says to advance the next item rather than end on a status report, and it stops when every item is done or one is recorded blocked with its reason. A plan that stops moving is a finding even while tool calls keep running. A finished dispatch arrives as an event with the verb it owes, and a continuation announced with nothing started is reported back. (#1487, #1490, #1498)
  • Fixed: a grown --help page silently disabled the structured-session lane. The help probe was capped at 16 KiB; claude --help reached 21,401 bytes with --verbose past the cut, so the negotiation refused a protocol the CLI does support, the spawn omitted --output-format stream-json, and every Claude unit ran with no token counts and no session id to steer with — visible only as an empty column. The help probe now gets a document-sized budget, a truncated read still answers the question when every flag was found in what was read, and a refusal states its reason. (#1499)
  • Setup, routing and models. Provider entitlements are asked as one plain ticked list with detected providers pre-ticked; the native-lane chain interview is offered during setup; capable, simple-work and deep-work join the model categories. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash onboarded with superseded generations retired from the shipped chains, and a vendor's dated snapshot id is recognized as the base alias it is a snapshot of. (#1465, #1468, #1469, #1479, #1493)
  • Windows fixes found through "flaky" tests. A sharing-denial retry for the store write that silently dropped a record, and store containment decided lexically instead of by two resolves. Both Windows shards run to completion, and a process-global interrupt flag is restored after every test that sets it — it had been showing up as a CI-only failure in whichever test ran next. (#1448, #1467, #1481, #1483)

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
oh-my-hermes 2.0.2 · stable

Everything merged since 2.0.1 (2026-09-05), 26 pull requests. The grouped summary is in CHANGELOG.md; the full list is below.

Why this release

omh update on an installer-managed 2.0.1 machine could stop with OMH update stopped during post_activation; the known-good generation remains active. and nothing else to act on. The staged self-update rendered the candidate workflow pack into its own generation, then re-entered the update against the real home, whose manifest still recorded the active generation's pack; every skill the catalog had changed since the last install was judged a "local modification", the re-entry refused without --force, and the whole update rolled back. Any machine whose recorded pack predated the candidate render hit it, which would have been every machine on the next version bump.

Highlights

  • The installer applies its local-modification and orphan-prune guards only to the directory the home manifest actually records, so a candidate generation is judged on its own content. A stopped update now prints the failing phase's reason, the generation it rolled back to, and the rerun; the re-entered update's stderr is captured for that reason and replayed. (#1377)
  • A transaction-level regression test drives the real CLI through the pack smoke and the post-activation re-entry against an older-manifest home, and a companion test proves the guard is what prevents the reported refusal. (#1378)
  • Release and update: a cut ends with the machine synced and a bare omh announces its Auto Update; omh --version and omh doctor expose a verifiable build identity; the cut stages the site badge it rewrites.
  • Coding and fanout: dispatch runs under an OS write fence proven per run; workspace targets by path shape; decode-to-fixpoint before a containment slot is charged; waits bind to the host's completion signal; cancelled is a first-class terminal state; an explicit user merge directive survives the delegation boundary.
  • Routing and models: Claude Mythos 5.1 leaves the shipped recommendation chains; the Codex Maestro defaults name the GPT generation the CLI serves.
  • Install and memory: the PowerShell installer reads the redirect Location header through a capability probe, proven on both PowerShell versions; memory credential boundaries hardened.

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.summary: Added a message gate: every coding delegation now shows which skill ran, which executor and model it ran on, what evidence class the answer belongs to, and a digest of the prompt behind it, rendered by OMH as exact lines instead of asked for in skill prose.…
gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
• Added a message gate: every coding delegation now shows which skill ran, which executor and model it ran on, what evidence class the answer belongs to, and a digest of the prompt behind it, rendered by OMH as exact lines instead of asked for in skill prose. The composed Hermes order ships as its own follow-on message, bounded and fenced.
  • Replaced the raw evidence vocabulary in everything a person reads. prepared_not_observed now renders as Plan · not run, completed as Code · reported done, and worktree_failed as Setup · failed, across chat, the status board, the route summary, the menu bar, and the README. The wire values are unchanged, so anything parsing them keeps working.
  • Separated an executor's own claim from a checked result: a unit that reported itself finished no longer renders identically to one that passed a gate.
  • Added omh goal status --text, so a goal ledger can be read as lines instead of escaped JSON.
  • Added a coding handoff safety boundary, a single safety preflight with an opt-in organization rule source, a task authority envelope, and risky-action classification with run-bound approval receipts.
  • Added external effect receipts, a normalized owner-progress vocabulary, safe blocked-work records with a decision history, and one shared append-only store with stale-update rejection.
  • Made unit prompts skill-aware: fan-out work discovers, arranges, and interviews the skills available to the executor it is handed to.
  • Gated follow-on engine starts on explicit user confirmation, and taught the delegate rules the real Claude Code permission-grant and session-resume mechanics.
  • Made the capability policy changeable and enforced rather than advisory.
  • Brought Windows to parity: the full suite runs on windows-latest in CI, journal lines stay LF, atomic replaces retry under sharing denials, and the installer path was fixed.
  • Added CI gates for roles, capability families, and whitespace, plus a catalog deference gate covering the sibling relationships the catalog writes in prose.
  • Bound observed workflows to snapshot evidence, and narrowed the plugin awareness markers to the routes they actually support.

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.summary: 1.0.4 - 2026-08-01 Overhauled Hermes memory into a governed lifecycle: admission, evaluation, retention, expiry, and retirement policies, write-replay hardening, migration with reactivation for legacy stores, rollup signals, peer-perspective records, and…
gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
1.0.4 - 2026-08-01

  • Overhauled Hermes memory into a governed lifecycle: admission, evaluation, retention, expiry, and retirement policies, write-replay hardening, migration with reactivation for legacy stores, rollup signals, peer-perspective records, and record fusion, plus recall packs with freshness, budget, and conflict-aware sibling controls.
  • Added a reviewed domain-intelligence store with an operator-controlled capture, review, approve, replace, and retire lifecycle, backed by descriptor-bound fail-closed snapshot validation and lineage, rejection, and retirement audit trails.
  • Added domain-aware clarification: after a project-local domain profile is approved, an unresolved chat question can ask the exact catalog-owned expert question (English or Korean) for eight specialist workflows, while every already-resolved route, dispatch, and protected body stays byte-identical.
  • Added eight specialist domain skills (sales development, finance analysis, legal compliance review, curriculum design, localization review, people ops, product brief, support operations) with domain-affinity ranking in the picker.
  • Added model inventory routing: setup captures which coding agents and models are actually installed, and routing, main-agent composition, and dispatch recommendations follow that inventory instead of assuming a fixed owner.
  • Added a research depth dial with declared shallow and deep chains, research-role routing, and a bounded executor prompt contract for prepared coding handoffs.
  • Reworked dispatch ergonomics: choice-required dispatch when several owners fit, a unit verification protocol for fan-out work, delegation-protocol guidance across surfaces, and session follow-up handoffs that keep context across turns.
  • Tightened routing quality with an accuracy program, overroute audits, picker-completion fixes, and clearer skill names and descriptions across the catalog.
  • Made omh update report package-version and content movement explicitly, refresh every installed surface, and bust stale caches.
  • Refreshed the README family with workflow GIFs, highlights, a uniform demo grid, and community links, and froze per-skill Korean copy behind explicit opt-in.

gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.summary: Hermes-native wrapper orchestration layer for Hermes Agent. 303 commits since v1.0.2. Install curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes/main/install.sh | sh omh setup Or ask your agent: Hey Agent, Install this >>…
gh-rlaope-oh-my-hermes.html:
Hermes-native wrapper orchestration layer for Hermes Agent. 303 commits since v1.0.2.

Install

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes/main/install.sh | sh
omh setup

Or ask your agent:

Hey Agent, Install this >> https://github.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes <<

Already installed?

omh update
omh doctor

Pinning this exact release instead of tracking main:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rlaope/oh-my-hermes/main/install.sh | OMH_CHANNEL=stable OMH_VERSION=1.0.3 sh

Highlights

Discovery and naming. A /omh meta-router gateway skill routes from the live catalog, four Hermes setup-guide skills ship with routed cards, and a generated full-catalog index reference makes the workflow surface discoverable from chat. Generated skill frontmatter now carries an omh- display prefix, so hermes skills list shows omh-routing, omh-plan, omh-doctor instead of bare names that could belong to any installed skill.

Bounded deep interview. Every interview question carries a Round {n}/6 header with a clarity percentage over three fixed dimensions, and the interview stops on resolution, an explicit user stop, or the round budget. Previously it had no round counter, no clarity signal, and an inherited rule that told the runtime to keep asking whenever an answer surfaced new ambiguity.

Coding delegation. Coding route next actions split into four request-led states, named coding-agent delivery takes precedence over advisor and feedback lanes, setup asks one question with usage-time owner delegation, and an opt-in local dispatch bridge executes fan-out contracts in parallel against a deterministic merge contract.

Messenger rendering. The chat route-hint path now honors the render-profile contract — the only limited-rendering path for the Hermes platforms not named individually — and a present-but-unsafe body warns instead of passing silently.

Operator signal. Wrapper degradation reaches chat users instead of being dropped at the wrapper, progress reporting detects claim/observation mismatches rather than only exempting them, and omh doctor gained a read-only advisory lane for the costliest Hermes misconfigurations, including a plugin that is installed but disabled.

Engineering gates. A pinned Ruff static-analysis gate runs in CI, a self-checking broad-exception policy gate classifies every broad except, repeated common-rail context in generated skills was measured and cut, and prompt, capability, stdout, and status payload budgets are bounded.

Defaults. Skill-pack install defaults to a core profile with opt-in full and a reconcile path back to core. All setup and CLI output defaults to English; localization is explicit opt-in via --language or OMH_LANG. OMH worktree creation was retired in favor of native Hermes and Git tooling.

See CHANGELOG.md for the full entry.

Verification

Release gates from docs/RELEASE.md were run locally and CI passed on Python 3.11 and 3.12: full suite 1860 passed; generated-doc byte gates green; harness validate 69 harnesses / 90 skills / 0 errors; release product-readiness --version 1.0.3 ready at score 100 with 0 blocking failures; use-case readiness 100; grounded-score 50/50; routing-precision 55/55; chat-card-coverage 60/60; route-hint-alignment 180/180 with 0 mismatch; context-brief 10/10; router-fast-path 11/11; localized-chat-copy 8/8; common-request-coverage 90/90; Hermes UX quality passed.

Install paths exercised: uv build plus wheel install with installed-console-script smoke; a live install.sh install into an isolated venv; and a live omh release hermes-smoke --live --install-path setup against a throwaway Hermes profile, which completed omh setup, hermes skills list --enabled-only, and omh doctor (28/28 checks) with the nine core omh- skills enabled.

Not observed: a live smoke against a maintainer's real Hermes profile, and any live Hermes chat session selecting OMH. These gates prove local deterministic contracts and an isolated install — they do not prove chat selection, executor dispatch, or message delivery.

Known issue in this tag

omh update on the preview channel reports main -> main instead of the version it moved between, because a branch archive records the source ref and not a version. Fixed on main after this tag (#670) — running omh update again picks up the fix and subsequent updates read 1.0.3 -> ….

gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.6.1 fixes one thing: reconnecting to a TV that got a new Wi-Fi address.

The problem

After a TV software update, or on a mesh Wi-Fi, a TV can get a new address. The app only tried the address it saved the first time, so Manage stayed "Offline" and waited for the TV forever, even with debugging switched on.

The fix

When the saved address doesn't answer, the app looks for the same TV on your Wi-Fi, the way "Add a TV" does, and saves its new address. It checks it's really your TV first (the TV must recognise this phone and have the same ID), so it never connects to another TV, and a TV that already trusted your phone doesn't ask you to allow it again.

Nothing else changes from 0.4.6.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.6.1.apk below and open it on your phone (Android 9 or newer, on the same Wi-Fi as the TV). It installs over 0.4.6 and keeps everything. If you're on the 0.4.7-beta1 test build, you already have this fix.

gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.6 gives Xiaomi and Redmi TVs on Google's Android TV home the new home screen, adds a one-tap "Report a problem" button, and makes the home screen switch safer, with fixes that came straight from testers' reports.

What's new

  • The new home screen on Xiaomi and Redmi TVs on Android 9, 10 and 11 that have no list of their own, such as the Mi TV 4i. Their setup wizard stays on and your Wi-Fi isn't touched. A Xiaomi TV with a home screen app you installed yourself gets it too, and your app stays installed.
  • Report a problem on every stop, timeout, paused change and connect problem. One tap opens a ready-filled GitHub issue in your browser, so there's nothing to paste. The app itself still sends nothing: nothing is public until you post it.
  • Run Setup again. If an earlier version left your home screen alone, for example before your TV had a list of its own, Manage now says so and offers to run Setup again.
  • Honest reasons. When another home screen app or a vendor service is why the app left the home screen alone, Setup and Manage say exactly that.

Safer home screen switch

  • TVs where a vendor service also answers the Home button keep their own home screen. One such TV failed to start after its home screen was switched in a test build.
  • On Xiaomi TVs, Mi TV+ and PatchWall's web content stay on while PatchWall stays on, because PatchWall can open at start-up. If an earlier version switched them off, Setup switches them back on before it changes the home screen.
  • Each time you open Manage, the app checks the Home button again and tells you if the TV's setup wizard could take it.
  • Right after the switch, if the TV brings up Live TV in front of the new home screen, the app presses Home again for you.

Fixes

  • Manage, the Restore point page and Done all show the restore point that "Undo everything" goes back to.
  • Manage no longer stays on "Working" after "Stop and undo".
  • Reports fold repeated connection retries into one line, so more of what happened fits.
  • The home screen switch no longer stops before it starts when the TV's screenshot is large (a 4K screen, or a detailed wallpaper). A safety check refused screenshots over 2 MB, nothing was changed, and the old home screen came back after a restart. Reports now also say which check stopped a switch, and why the TV refused a step.

Known issue

  • On some TVs (seen on Xiaomi and TCL with Android 11, and Android 14 boxes) Android doesn't let the app copy the look and wallpaper into the new home screen. The new home screen works with its default look, nothing else changes, and the fix comes in 0.4.7.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.6.apk below and open it on an Android 9 or newer phone with a screen lock, on the same Wi-Fi as your Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV. It installs over any earlier version, including the 0.4.6 test builds, and keeps everything. If the app opens Manage for your TV, tap Run Setup again to use what's new.

Clean Your TV app 0.4.5 brings the 3.0 home screen from Gathin's Clean Your TV, more choices in the Look sheet, 25 more TV lists (173 in all), and fixes for phones on Android 9 to 12 that could not connect to a new TV.

What's new

  • Home screen 3.0. A TV that has the home screen from an earlier version sees "Update the home screen" in Manage. Nothing changes until you tap it, and the update keeps your look, your dock and your remote buttons.
  • More Look options on home screen 3.0: every app in one row, a dock with no band, the greeting on or off, the date under the clock, a brighter date, a warning colour on the Wi-Fi icon when the internet is down, app tiles as icons on cards, and a rim or halo highlight. The preview shows each one before anything reaches the TV, and looks you already sent stay exactly as they are.
  • 25 more TV lists from Clean Your TV, among them NVIDIA SHIELD TV (2017), Philips Google TV TA1 and TA7, Sony BRAVIA VU1 and VU3, TCL G08 (EU, Android 12), OnePlus TV (Cebu and Dosa), Xiaomi Mi Box S (Android 12) and several Xiaomi Mi TVs. The Sony BRAVIA BF1 list now matches BF1 sets, and lists we already had got their contributors' fixes.
  • Better back on. If this app switched off something a TV's list now keeps on, like a TCL remote's mic service, Manage says so and offers to switch it back on.
  • PatchWall on Xiaomi TVs is now your choice, so the remote's PatchWall button keeps working.

Fixes

  • Phones on Android 9 to 12 can connect to a new TV again. The TV never showed Allow and the app said "unreachable". Saving a restore file on phones below Android 15 is fixed too.
  • Some TCL Smart TV Pro sets on Google TV got a list made for the Android TV version, so the app left their home screen alone. They now get the right set.
  • Connection errors say what went wrong instead of "unreachable". A TV that leaves the Wi-Fi mid-run pauses the run instead of hanging.
  • "Try again" after a home screen check that timed out now really tries again, and the last screen says honestly when the home screen stayed.
  • Safer undo: "Undo everything" is no longer refused for protected apps, never switches accessibility on, and never treats a chooser screen as your home screen.

gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.0 brings a new Look sheet for your TV's home screen: pick a picture, one of five styles and how many apps sit in a row, and see your own TV in a preview before anything reaches it.

What's new

  • Five styles, each shown as a small preview of your TV with your picture: Classic (a dark dock, a big name and a soft glow), Glass (a frosted dock and light in each app's colour), Spotlight (a big banner of the app you are on, with the app's colour across the top), All apps (every app in one grid) and Calm (no glow and no big name, just apps and your picture).
  • Pictures for any style: Mist, Aurora, Navy, Autumn lake, Curtains, Mountains (with a sky that changes with the hour), Lamp light, Neon, Cobalt, no picture, or your own photo, cropped on the phone. Diwali is there until 10 November, with its lamps and festive icons. The pictures are our own work, free to use (CC0).
  • 4 to 8 apps in a row. Fewer apps means bigger tiles. "Names under every app" puts each app's name under its tile, easier to read from the sofa.
  • More options: how the highlight moves (Lively, Smooth, Quick or Off), the big name, the glow, a ring in the app's colour, the dock band (solid, see-through or glass), the buttons at the top and a green Wi-Fi icon. Advanced has lift and zoom, see-through amount, sky strength and the settings file itself.
  • Nothing is sent until you tap "Put it on the TV". "Undo changes" takes the sheet back to how it opened, and "Put back the earlier look" brings back the look the TV had before your last send.
  • Your dock keeps its order when you go to fewer apps in a row, and empty spaces stay empty on the TV.
  • Setup's Look step is the same sheet, with Done at the bottom.
  • A look you picked before this version stays on the TV exactly as it is until you send a new one.
  • TCL: picking TCL under "Change model" now asks whether the TV's menus are in English (or your language) or in Chinese, so TCL TVs sold outside China get the right steps to connect.

Clean Your TV app 0.3.6 fixes TVs that got stuck after a home screen switch rolled back and the install that kept saying the TV stopped answering. Thank you to everyone who sent a report and a log: each of these fixes starts from one.

What's new

  • No more stuck Setup after a rollback. When the home screen switch rolled back, Setup offered "Try with the wizard off", which saved a choice that every later plan refused, and Back led to Welcome instead of the TV's restore options. That card is gone, saved choices the TV would refuse are dropped before planning, and Back on a refused plan opens Manage for a TV this app already changed (#375, #385).
  • No more endless "TV stopped answering" during an install. Some TVs end the app's install with an error while staying connected. The app now checks whether the install landed: done if it did, otherwise that step fails and Setup carries on with the clean-up, without the home screen switch (#80, #364, #367).
  • A heads-up on TCL Google TV. Before the switch, the plan screen and Manage > Home screen say that the remote's Settings (gear), Netflix and YouTube buttons don't work with the new home screen, and that Use the TV's own home screen brings them back (#275).
  • A stricter safety rule for the setup wizard. The home screen switch is never planned while the TV shows a setup wizard that can take the Home button and the switch would leave it on, also on TVs with an exact list such as the Sony BRAVIA BF1. Those TVs get the clean-up alone. The TCL G10 Google TV list switches the wizard off as part of the switch, so it keeps its switch.
  • Reports list what was switched off. The problem report now has "Switched off by this app", so a reply can say exactly what to put back.
  • Better logs, and Copy error. The diagnostics log now says why a connection failed, what the TV showed when the home check rolled back, and the step the switch stopped at. When the TV answers but the phone can't connect, the door says what on the phone can block the app (a per-app network limit on MIUI or Samsung, a VPN, Private DNS, mobile data) and offers Copy error: a short summary with no addresses in it, ready to paste into an issue.

gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.5 gives more TVs a careful clean-up and adds a safety guard for the ACER R4G. Thank you to everyone who sent a TV report: the list of apps in each one showed us what is safe to switch off on TVs nobody has tested yet.

What's new

  • More TVs get a careful clean-up. TVs from brands with one or two tested lists (Skyworth, SHARP, onn, OnePlus, Haier and others) now switch off up to six hidden feedback and advertising services: Google Feedback and its consent prompt, the print service, and Android's on-device advertising, ad personalization and ad model services. Before, these TVs got no clean-up unless a list matched the exact model (#89, #108, #169, #194, #196, #251).
  • Nothing else changes on those TVs. The home screen decision is the same as before, and the app still checks each switch-off on the TV before it runs it. TVs that already had a brand set get nothing new.
  • A safety guard for the ACER R4G. It is made by MOKA, in the same family as the TVs whose setup wizard comes back at every restart, so Setup never offers the home screen switch on it and does the clean-up alone (#74, #102).
  • Reports say which set was used. A TV report from one of these TVs now says Profile: brand set <Brand> instead of none.

gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.4 fixes "plan refused" on TVs whose home screen was already changed by another tool, and makes Setup honest when it can't make a safe plan. Thank you to everyone who sent a report with the log: it showed us exactly where it went wrong.

What's new

  • A home screen installed another way is left as it is. Some TVs already had the new home screen from the Clean Your TV tool for computers, which signs it with a different key. Setup used to stop with "plan refused" on every try. Now it leaves that home screen as it is and does the clean-up (#171, #187, #220).
  • An honest message when there is no safe plan. Setup used to say "We couldn't read what's on the TV" even though the TV had answered. Now it says it couldn't make a plan it is sure is safe, that nothing was changed, and Report a problem sends us the reason (#82, #99, #45).
  • Manage explains it too. On those TVs, Home screen says Setup left the home screen as it was, instead of offering a dock and a look for it.
  • Reports name the reason. The diagnostics log now says why a plan was refused. Apps you installed yourself are never named.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.3 fixes the issues people reported on the app's first public day. Thank you all: every report made this release better.

What's new

  • A TV that keeps something on no longer stops Setup. Some TVs answer "yes" when the app switches an app off, then keep it on. Setup now skips it, runs the rest of the clean-up, and Done names what wouldn't switch off. Before, Carry on met the same step again every time (#10).
  • Your own launcher is safe. A launcher you installed yourself is never switched off. If the TV's home screen was already changed, by another app or an earlier change, Setup leaves it as it is and does the clean-up, instead of "plan refused" (#8).
  • Honest Done screens. When nothing was changed, Done says so, and why (#15).
  • Manage explains the home screen. On a TV that kept its own home screen, Manage says why and what would change it, instead of a dock and a look that ended in "We stopped" (#3).
  • Reports fill the form in for you. Help add this TV and Report a problem now put the report straight into the GitHub form, and the report box can't be posted empty (#12, #14, #16).
  • Build numbers like "V816.0.11.0" are no longer masked as network addresses in reports.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.2 fixes the first issues people reported, and makes it easy to report a problem or a TV the app doesn't know yet. Thank you to everyone who took the time to write in.

What's new

  • Fire TV sets are recognised on their own. Fire TV and Fire TV Edition TVs (Insignia, Toshiba and others) are now recognised from the TV's own details, even when the app has no list for the exact model. They get the clean-up only: Fire OS doesn't let another home screen take over, so the app no longer tries (#2).
  • Undo can't get stuck any more. Undo now checks the TV itself: if the TV's own home screen is back, undo is done, even when the TV refuses a step that is already in place. If 0.3.1 left you on "The setup didn't finish", it clears the next time the app connects to the TV after updating.
  • A way out, always. Stop here shows Done only once the run has really stopped, and "Forget this TV" ends an unfinished setup for that TV.
  • Help add this TV. When the app doesn't know your TV yet, one tap makes a short report of what the TV is and which apps it came with. Apps you installed yourself are only counted, never named. You read the whole text first, then paste it into a pre-filled GitHub form or share it another way. The app sends nothing itself (#1).
  • Report a problem, in Settings and on the screens where something went wrong, does the same with the app's log. The log is now readable: plain error names, how the TV was matched, and the step that failed with the TV's answer.
  • Privacy: the policy now describes these reports and the app's own log, which "Delete everything" also clears. Nothing new is collected.

Clean Your TV app 0.3.0 gets the app ready for Google Play and F-Droid. If you install from GitHub, nothing changes in use: same app, same features.

  • One reproducible release for every store. Each release is built twice and compared byte for byte, for both the GitHub/F-Droid APK and the Google Play bundle. F-Droid's own build of this release matches the APK below exactly.
  • A website and a privacy policy: https://udhaykumarbala.github.io/cleanyourtv-app/ (download, the three steps, supported TVs, how to install an APK) and https://udhaykumarbala.github.io/cleanyourtv-app/privacy/ (no data collected, no accounts, no analytics).

gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.summary: The first public release of Clean Your TV app, a community-built phone app for Clean Your TV. gh-udhaykumarbala-cleanyourtv-app.html:
The first public release of Clean Your TV app, a community-built phone app for Clean Your TV. Anyone can now clean up an Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV from an Android phone: no laptop, no coding agent, no cables. The app switches off adverts, tracking and preloaded apps, installs the calm Clean Your TV home screen with a dock of the apps you use, shows its progress on the TV, and keeps a restore point so every change can be put back.

Highlights

  • 131 community tested TV profiles from 46 brands, plus a careful brand fallback for models nobody has profiled yet.
  • Launcher 2.5 (upstream v2.5.0): edit the dock from the remote, rows and wallpaper in Launcher settings, and more. A dock changed on the TV survives a new look from the phone.
  • A plan first. See what will be switched off and what is kept; Customise shows every command in order before it runs.
  • Restore point and undo, one app or everything, plus a restore copy with plain scripts that work from any computer with adb.
  • A watchdog on the TV puts its own home screen back if the phone does not confirm the new one within 150 seconds.
  • Stricter safety: the app never switches off what drives the HDMI and tuner inputs, accessibility or the remote, and on TVs where switching the home screen is known to cause trouble (Chromecast with Google TV, the Google TV Streamer, some Kalley and PRISM+ sets, TVs whose setup wizard must stay on) it does the clean-up only and says why.
  • No accounts, no analytics; internet only to GitHub, and only when you ask.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

v0.1.5 · 25 changes from 5 contributors

Highlights

Turn a No project thread into a project. Use Claude and GPT models and thinking controls with Antigravity. Customize thread details, including usage limits. Switch all your installations between Stable and Nightly in one step.

  • New threads avoid providers that just hit usage limits (#26234)
  • Guest links no longer expose file diffs (#26538)

  • Antigravity file reads no longer keep spinning (#26928)
  • Copilot follow-ups no longer kill background agents (#26715)

T3 Code Orchestrator V2 is now stable

v0.1.0 is the first stable release of T3 Code Orchestrator V2, which has been in Nightly since early October. V2 rebuilds the part of T3 Code that runs your agents: how turns start, stop, queue, and resume; how subagents and background work are tracked; how threads move between providers; and how history is saved. Read "Before you update" if you use the mobile app or OpenCode.

The short version
  • Pi, Muse Code and OpenCode 2 support
  • delegate_task: an agent can start child agents on any provider or model and wait for their results. This is the way to use several harnesses together.
  • Fork any thread
  • Switch provider or model mid-thread, with caveats (see below)
  • The T3 Code MCP: agents can create, launch, message, wait on, read, search, and interrupt threads
  • ACP Registry: add any registry agent (Devin, Cline, Kimi, Droid, and more)
  • Cursor runs on the official Cursor SDK instead of the CLI
  • A real server-side queue: queued messages survive restarts, and you can steer or queue each message
  • Subagents you can follow: every child shows up with its model, status, and results
  • Interrupted threads continue after a restart
  • Auto-resume when usage limits reset
  • Scheduled tasks
Highlights

Agents that manage agents

  • delegate_task lets an agent hand work to a child agent on any provider and model, with its own options and role. Each child runs as its own thread, keeps its own provider-native history, and reports a result. The parent can wait for children or keep working, and it wakes up when they finish, with results batched together. This is the recommended way to combine harnesses, for example Claude planning and Codex implementing.

  • The T3 Code MCP gives agents tools to create, launch, message, wait on, read, search, and interrupt threads. They can also:

    • fork and merge back;
    • edit and reorder queues;
    • answer questions;
    • rename threads, regenerate titles, link pull requests, and settle threads;
    • manage scheduled tasks and projects;
    • hand work off to a worktree;
    • list and close previews.

    Agents can't approve their own permission requests.

  • Attach another thread as context: type @ and the thread's name, or drag a thread from the sidebar into the composer.

Fork any thread

  • Fork from any finished run, including failed, interrupted, and limited ones. Forks stay on the same provider by default and use the provider's native fork where it has one (Codex, Claude, Pi, OpenCode 2), so the full history comes along. When you're done, merge the fork's context back into its source.

Switching providers mid-thread

  • You can change provider, account, model, or options between turns, and queue a switch without stopping the current turn. Per-provider and per-model options are remembered.

[!WARNING] Switching providers is supported, but it isn't the recommended way to use multiple harnesses. The handoff is lossy. The new provider gets a budgeted selection of the conversation's messages, but not the previous provider's reasoning, its tool calls and results, or attachments. The agent can look up omitted messages, but the working state the first provider built up doesn't carry over. To get another harness's help, have the agent use delegate_task instead. Changing model or options within the same provider usually continues the provider's own session, so nothing is lost.

Subagents and background work you can see

  • Native subagents from Claude, Codex, OpenCode 2, Cursor, and Pi show as child threads in a lineage view, with their model, status, progress, results, and duration. Several subagents fold into one collapsible card, and the mobile app has an agents sheet.
  • When background work finishes, the agent wakes up and says which subagent, command, or monitor finished.
  • Stop works on background work too, including after the foreground turn has finished.
  • After a restart, T3 Code tells the agent which background work died, and threads that lost background work can continue.

More providers, and deeper support

  • Pi, including Pi 1.0: native resume, fork, rollback, and steering; skills, extensions, and extension dialogs; T3 Code tools inside Pi; and permission modes Pi enforces itself.

  • OpenCode 2 (2.0.18+):

    • native steering, forks, rollback, compaction, and plan mode;
    • child sessions as subagent threads;
    • T3 Code tools injected into the server;
    • recovery after restarts.

    T3 Code detects whether you run 1.x or 2.x. OpenCode 1.x keeps the support it had in V1, plus forking.

  • ACP Registry: search the official registry and install an agent on the server you choose, with shared sign-in across your devices.

  • Cursor on the official SDK: browser sign-in, model discovery, project skills and rules, images, plans, and resuming local agents.

  • Many fixes for Claude, Codex, Grok, and Antigravity. Questions, plans, and todos work again, along with compaction and resume. Subagent output stays in the right thread, and approvals route correctly.

A queue you can trust

  • The queue lives on the server and keeps its order across restarts. After a restart it waits for you to resume it. It also survives usage limits.
  • Edit, reorder, remove, and steer queued messages, including their attachments. This works on mobile too.
  • Choose whether a follow-up message steers the running turn or queues: Settings → General → Follow-up behavior. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter does the opposite of your default.

Limits and recovery

  • Threads stopped by a usage limit show as Limited. Resume manually, resume at reset, or snooze until reset.
  • With Settings → General → Continue threads after restarts on, interrupted threads continue after an update, crash, or reboot.
  • A live context meter, plus usage that stays correct through compaction and session changes.

Scheduled tasks

  • Create, edit, pause, resume, run, and delete automations on web and mobile, filtered by project and environment. Fixed schedules use the server's time zone.

Thread details and the sidebar

  • Workspace, Git, scripts, linked pull requests, automations, and lineage now live in a thread-details panel. Merge controls follow the current checks.
  • Sidebar status reflects what's actually running: working, waiting, limited, or failed. Settling is handled by the server and accounts for linked PRs, pins, and background work.
  • Working section (beta): busy threads stay out of the way until they need you.
  • Configurable worktree branch names, per project if you like.

Faster and lighter

  • Long conversations load in pages.
  • Streaming updates are batched, and the app re-renders less.
  • Memory use is lower, and mobile scrolls more smoothly.
Before you update
  • Your threads come with you, but it's a one-way copy. The first time V2 starts, it copies your existing database and imports your threads. The previous version keeps its own copy, and changes made in one version don't show up in the other. See "Moving from V1 to V2" in the pinned issue.
  • Update every app you connect with. A V2 server and a V1 app can't talk to each other. Whichever side is older refuses the connection and tells you which machine to update. Update every machine that runs a T3 Code server, including background services and remote machines you connect to, and every desktop app you use.
  • The mobile app must be updated too.

cmux.summary: Highlights Workspace groups — select sidebar workspaces and press ⌘⇧G to group them under a collapsible header, with an anchor workspace, drag-to-group, in-group reorder, per-group color/icon, header unread badges, and a cmux workspace-group CLI namespace.…
cmux.html:
Highlights

  • Workspace groups — select sidebar workspaces and press ⌘⇧G to group them under a collapsible header, with an anchor workspace, drag-to-group, in-group reorder, per-group color/icon, header unread badges, and a cmux workspace-group CLI namespace.
  • Focus & Recently Closed history — navigate back/forward through recently focused workspaces and windows from the titlebar, and reopen closed surfaces from a searchable history pane.
  • Agent Hibernation — pause idle agent sessions and restore them on demand to cut background resource use.
  • Detachable SSH PTY daemon — keeps remote sessions alive across reconnects.
  • Configurable sidebar and tab bar font sizes, redesigned notifications popover (swipe to dismiss), browser tab mute, Fork Conversation menu, Xcode-style project visualizer pane, and a cmux diff CodeView viewer.
  • Fixes across file preview, Hermes hooks, split zoom, titlebar controls, Vault resume, and equalize splits.

openwork.html:
Bring Claude conversations into OpenWork

  • Bring your Claude history with you. Import Claude chats and Claude Code sessions into a workspace from Settings → Import, where they become regular OpenWork chats.
  • Work with connected files on OpenCode v2. Bring Google Drive, OneDrive, and SharePoint files into your workspace and save edits back; attach workspace files to Gmail drafts and replies, or upload them to Google Drive. OpenWork asks you to approve each transfer.
  • Use computer use on Windows and set it up once. Windows desktop users can use computer use with apps on This PC. Set it up in Settings → Computer use; chats no longer have a computer status button, and the browser has one button in the side rail.
  • Desktop work keeps its place and gets easier to start. The window reopens at its previous size and position, Cmd+N (Ctrl+N) starts a session even while you type, and organization switching refreshes your skills, connected apps, and models. Verified sign-in no longer waits for organization discovery to finish. Show model reasoning now starts off; turn it on in Settings → Preferences to see readable reasoning.
  • For admins: completed features are now available by default, with clearer controls. Local AI providers, Automation settings, agent-assisted connection removal, Workbot search, improved usage-limit cards, task-preserving sign-in, Claude imports, and organization Prompts are available without a special setup; retired OpenCode Zen models are no longer offered. Automations are on by default, with separate Desktop and Cloud controls for organizations; sandbox join links add admins by default, with a choice to add members instead.
  • Workbot, models, and self-hosted setups are more dependable. Workbot handles brief sign-in interruptions and rebuilds outdated computers when resumed. OpenWork Models adds GPT-6.1 Terra, Kimi K3.1 Pro, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; self-hosted desktops no longer update beyond the server's supported release.

Work with OneDrive and SharePoint files in OpenWork

  • Work with OneDrive and SharePoint files. Agents can search, open, edit, and save Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files, including files shared with you, once an admin enables the required permission.
  • Workbot's Browser and Computer views connect again. If a computer needs an update, Workbot rebuilds it when you open the view; it avoids rebuilding while a task is running.
  • Sign-in and connected admin tools are safer. The desktop app now blocks unsafe non-web links from remote MCP sign-in requests.   • For admins and self-hosters: Den gets security and recovery fixes. Self-hosted Den deployments should update for recent Next.js security fixes, and opt-in administrator permission recovery now works with common database encodings. openwork.html:
Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere

  • Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere. Desktop users can pop the computer view and floating browser into their own windows above other apps, and browser full screen now fills the display.
  • Dictate messages and use workspace commands again. On macOS and Windows, dictation shows your words as you speak, stops when you click the mic again, and keeps words across pauses. On OpenCode v2, / lists workspace commands and skills, and picking one runs it.
  • Follow Workbot's browser work and longer tasks. Workbot shows browser activity live and links to pages it opened. Background tasks can pass files and read just the part they need, while longer scripts and documents can finish without a cut-off reply being mistaken for completed work.
  • Invitations and connections take clearer paths. Invited teammates can join their workspace during sign-in, invitation emails explain who invited them and where to get help, and completed MCP sign-ins no longer appear to fail. Teams messages and Outlook meeting invitations now wait for your confirmation.
  • For admins: organization and billing details are clearer. Compact organization rows, recent organizations, and week-over-week summaries make admin pages easier to scan. The Free plan covers up to five users, and pending invitations count until they expire.
  • For self-hosters: web access and standalone installs are more predictable. openwork-server web answers only its own host names unless you add proxy names with --allowed-hosts. Standalone server and bootstrap installs require Node.js 24.x (24.22.1 or newer), and the bootstrap installer downloads a supported runtime when needed.

openwork.summary: Move older OpenWork installs to OpenCode v2 in the background Older installs move to OpenCode v2 in the background. Existing installs still using OpenCode v1 are moved over automatically, with a backup made first so your chats are kept. Windows installers also…
openwork.html:
Move older OpenWork installs to OpenCode v2 in the background

  • Older installs move to OpenCode v2 in the background. Existing installs still using OpenCode v1 are moved over automatically, with a backup made first so your chats are kept. Windows installers also carry less duplicate engine data, and Windows can identify OpenWork's signed app files.
  • Computer use is more capable and predictable. For Mac users, the agent can script apps directly and keeps working while you use your computer; Take over and Stop return control, and Continue resumes the task. Workbot can also script supported desktop apps. Browser pages keep a steady desktop, tablet, or phone size while the panel changes, and forms take fewer steps. When available, you can dictate into OpenWork or Workbot.
  • Chat can work with more of your existing tasks and connections. Type # to add another task as context, ask the agent to create or move sidebar groups, and find connected actions with everyday wording. You can finish or repair an API-key connection in chat without sharing the key with the agent, and OpenWork Cloud tools work again in older desktop versions.
  • Documents and first launches are more dependable. Closing an edited document now gives clear save, discard, or cancel choices, and reloading or reopening it preserves your editing session and unsaved work. Workbot can open a requested document beside chat, explain why a file could not open, and show or rebuild a computer that will not connect. Fresh desktop installs can load built-in tools even if the package registry is unavailable; slow Windows sign-in and first launch no longer hide recovery options.
  • For admins: team and organization controls are clearer. Platform administrators can manage feature access per organization member and, when enabled, grant organizations Web access or extra Free Auto usage. Admins can finish connector setup after a check fails, remove connectors, and save team-role changes reliably; Workbot settings show one default model and its availability. When available, Workbot can guide eligible people from free Auto to paid Luna without losing the conversation.
  • Website visitors can find practical AI governance guidance. The expanded enterprise pages explain governing employee AI and planning an OpenWork rollout.
