openwork.summary: Read, edit, and discuss documents in Workbot Work on documents without leaving Workbot. When Documents is enabled for your workspace, preview Drive files before choosing Edit when editing is enabled, keep chat open beside a document, and continue your…
openwork.html:
Read, edit, and discuss documents in Workbot

  • Work on documents without leaving Workbot. When Documents is enabled for your workspace, preview Drive files before choosing Edit when editing is enabled, keep chat open beside a document, and continue your conversation with the file in view. Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides stay in Google and save to the original; on OpenWork Cloud, Office files can use an editor in your own workspace when enabled.
  • AI models and providers work more smoothly across OpenWork. Desktop users can use existing Azure Foundry and custom OpenAI-compatible providers on OpenCode v2, see organization model changes in the picker when enabled, and find the same available models in Settings and shortcuts. When AI Gateway access is enabled, cloud agents can use supported models assigned by their organization.
  • Admins can check setup before work gets stuck. Settings › Diagnostics brings desktop startup, AI provider, connector, and deployment-service checks together. Google Workspace settings can also identify APIs an admin needs to turn on, and Workbot explains when an organization needs an AI provider before it can answer.
  • Chat keeps files, prompts, and agent work on track. Files saved from chat go to the opened folder, including files created in a conversation's own folder; links with spaces open correctly, failed writes are labeled as failed, and messages in side chats are easier to start. OpenCode v2 history copies can resume after restart; if a chat is too large to copy whole, its largest outputs or attachments stay in the original history.
  • Team and Workbot tasks have clearer paths. When enabled, members can connect assigned accounts in Workbot; members with team-management access can open the right team's settings, and teams can follow tasks started on another computer. When available, admins can set team or organization defaults for new desktop chats and provider-specific spend limits, and inspect Library use and free Auto conversion insights. Workbot's link-only sharing is gone; authorized invitation emails remain available in Den.
  • Self-hosting and connected tools get practical fixes. Self-hosters get updated AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure deployment options and clearer service checks. MCP clients can identify OpenWork and receive clearer tool guidance, and the website's Trust Center links now lead to the hosted Trust Center.

openwork.title: OpenWork v0.18.58
openwork.summary: Run OpenWork Web on your own self-hosted deployment Self-host OpenWork Web and team tools on AWS. For self-hosters: run OpenWork Web with sandboxed browser workspaces, and deploy Slack, Workbot, and Automations that run without a desktop. AWS deployments can…
openwork.html:
Run OpenWork Web on your own self-hosted deployment

  • Self-host OpenWork Web and team tools on AWS. For self-hosters: run OpenWork Web with sandboxed browser workspaces, and deploy Slack, Workbot, and Automations that run without a desktop. AWS deployments can use existing networks and load balancers, and can connect to an existing cluster or runner fleet.
  • Connect OpenCode 2 to your organization. If you use OpenWork from OpenCode: the opencode-openwork plugin brings in your organization's AI Gateway models, tools, and skills after sign-in, without the desktop app. You can also upgrade desktop chats to OpenCode 2 with a backup first; its conversations can use the built-in browser and discover connected tools reliably.
  • Admins get clearer controls and reporting. Organization Analytics is back, with restored usage and workflow history where available. When enabled, admins can also report on skills, plugins, and connectors, set member, admin, and team permissions, and choose a default model for cloud agents; Audit Logs now cover more organization activity.
  • Chat and daily work recover more smoothly. Pasted text and images stay at the cursor, reopened Apps load their data, migrated chats with a missing agent can answer again, and OpenWork keeps the Working status visible during quiet stretches. Ollama keeps multiple selected models and their thinking choices; Drive uploads respect your chosen Google account.
  • Calendar, Workbot, and connections do more. When Calendar features are enabled, add or edit Automations alongside meetings; Workbot can recover stopped tasks. When enabled, admins can check when connections were last verified, and compatible MCP clients can subscribe to remote-session updates.
  • Some familiar pages and searches have changed. Organization dashboards and admin-assigned dashboards in Desktop are gone, while personal dashboards remain. “Search sessions” now searches session titles and workspace names, not message text; for organizations with OpenWork Models, Auto is replaced in the model picker by GPT-6 Luna.

openwork.html:
Move your Claude Cowork setup to OpenWork with one prompt

  • Move your Cowork setup with one prompt. Ask the agent you already use to follow openworklabs.com/migrate.md to bring your Claude Cowork and Claude Code plugins and skills into OpenWork. Re-running picks up changes without duplicates, reuses connections your organization already has, and explains when a connection still needs setup.
  • Give each teammate their own connector key. For admins: external connections can use individual keys instead of one shared key. Members can add or replace their key from the Library or Den, using a masked entry form; desktop chat can guide them to add one when needed. For admins who use LiteLLM, connecting your own proxy is also available as a preview on request.
  • Auto and Apps are available to more organizations. Free Auto no longer needs an organization-by-organization rollout, and every organization can build Apps without a platform admin enabling them. Auto can also read images you attach or that tools return, and signed-out Linux desktops no longer need a system keyring to use it.
  • Self-hosting gains a Google Cloud Run starting point. For self-hosters: starter deployment files and instructions cover the Den API, Den web app, and migration job on Cloud Run. Old self-hosted Den settings that had no effect are no longer read.
  • Everyday work is clearer and more dependable. Your first organization message now gets an answer before you have a workspace; videos made in a conversation's work folder play in chat; and stopping a run no longer leaves a bold “Step interrupted” row. Agent-led installs open on Setup complete without requiring Node first, and teammate invites survive workspace claiming. Model names and provider details are clearer. Workbot uses one quiet activity line and can react with emoji, while Slack runs wait for slow desktop work instead of reporting that they are stuck.
  • Some desktop options have changed or are gone. Workspace sharing and remote-workspace connections have been removed. Organization Analytics is gone, while usage reporting remains in AI Gateway. Plugins now come from your organization's Library instead of being installed into workspaces, and the “From GitHub” plugin import is gone. The Library no longer has a card view. Automation choices now say Desktop or Cloud, and computer use has been removed from that editor.

Workflows and artifacts can use your connected tools

  • Connected tools work in Workflows and artifacts. Live artifacts, on-demand Workflows, and scheduled Automations can now use connection tools and perform write actions. Large tool inputs, such as Notion database queries, also work.
  • Work sent to your desktop reports back. If you use OpenWork from Slack or another connected app, you can now follow a desktop task's progress, read its conversation, send a follow-up, or stop it. Slack reports the result in the original thread, and tasks appear as normal chats using your chosen model.
  • Auto works in more situations. Eligible organization members can use Auto alongside other models, and signed-out Auto is available to OpenWork builds and compatible clients. Deployments can disable Auto while keeping other models available.
  • Chat and the built-in browser are clearer and more dependable. Model choices explain why a model is unavailable; OpenCode v2 now shows a Connect card when a service needs sign-in. The browser explains when a page cannot connect and offers Reload, and HTML file previews are isolated from the rest of OpenWork.
  • For admins and self-hosters: Admins can choose “Only models you provide,” enable Slack progress updates, and review free Auto usage. Self-hosters can deploy with draft Terraform modules for AWS ECS Fargate or Kubernetes, including an existing ECS cluster.
  • Other changes: OpenWork-built items are now called artifacts. Browser login sync and its setup controls are gone; sign in directly in the built-in browser. Organization-managed Dashboards are disabled by default and must be enabled per organization.

openwork.title: OpenWork v0.18.54
openwork.summary: Enterprise sign-in and version pinning are back, plus Amazon Bedrock and model shortcuts This release covers everything since v0.18.52. v0.18.53 was never published, so its changes are included here. Organization sign-in and allowed versions work again.…
openwork.html:
Enterprise sign-in and version pinning are back, plus Amazon Bedrock and model shortcuts

This release covers everything since v0.18.52. v0.18.53 was never published, so its changes are included here.

  • Organization sign-in and allowed versions work again. OpenWork Enterprise and OpenWork Cloud desktops once again ask people to sign in to their organization before they start working, and desktop updates skip any version an admin removed from Allowed desktop versions. Other desktop policies stay saved but are not enforced on the desktop while they are redesigned.
  • Amazon Bedrock in AI Gateway. For admins: add Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock (OpenAI) with an AWS region and access keys, and reuse the saved keys for the second one. Anthropic effort choices are kept through the gateway.
  • Switch models with a key. In Settings › Keyboard shortcuts you can bind a key to a saved model with its reasoning level and Fast. ⌃⇧F (Ctrl+Alt+F on Windows and Linux) turns Fast on or off, and the model name shows "· Fast" while it's on.
  • Chat keeps its place. Editing a message while a reply is running replaces it instead of queueing the edit. Conversations stay in their folder when an agent changes directory, and questions and approvals no longer disappear. You can switch between OpenCode engines from the command palette and choose whether to copy older chats across. Agent tool work is summarized by what it did instead of raw tool names.
  • Simpler connector setup. For admins in OpenWork Cloud: API-key, custom sign-in, Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 connectors use the new setup flow and can be edited in place, and Plugins has clearer filters. Apps like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can connect to OpenWork Connect without registering first, failed sign-ins explain what to do next, and the MCP docs have one-click Cursor and VS Code install links.
  • Also in this release. Windows installers are published again. Updating no longer fails with a checksum error after a release is re-run. Update controls in Settings are more compact, a second OpenWork profile no longer stops the first one's engine, and the website shows OpenWork's completed SOC 2 Type II audit.

Self-hosted upgrades from v0.18.46 or earlier: this release applies database migrations 0095–0110. Stop den-api/den-web writers first, then run helm upgrade with --set migrations.writersStoppedFor0097=true --timeout 30m (and without --reuse-values). See the den-db README for details.

openwork.title: OpenWork v0.18.52
openwork.summary: Manage your Library from the desktop, find anything from one + menu, and a rebuilt AI Gateway Your Library works fully on the desktop. You can now add, share, edit and delete skills, connectors and plugins without leaving the app. A new Connectors tab lists…
openwork.html:
Manage your Library from the desktop, find anything from one + menu, and a rebuilt AI Gateway

  • Your Library works fully on the desktop. You can now add, share, edit and delete skills, connectors and plugins without leaving the app. A new Connectors tab lists your connectors, adding one starts from a catalog with service logos, and an MCP server's address is checked before it's saved. Each item's page has Chat, which starts a task with that item ready to use, and Share on items you own. When a skill shapes an answer, chat names the skill. Signed out, the Library shows one clear Sign in to OpenWork Cloud button instead of an "Add to library" button that did nothing. Lists also load faster.
  • One + menu in the composer finds everything. The paperclip and tools buttons are now a single + menu that opens on a search across your files, skills, connectors, plugins and commands. It still finds what you meant when you make a typo ("hubsopt" finds HubSpot). Attaching a file is the first option, or press ⌘U (Ctrl+U on Windows and Linux).
  • Usage limits are clearer. When you reach your organization's usage limit, the chat says which limit you hit and when it resets, and you can ask for more right there. The account menu shows how much of each limit you have left, and the new Settings › Usage page has the details. The chat no longer also shows a misleading "too many requests" error under the limit.
  • AI Gateway is rebuilt and available to every organization. For admins: AI Gateway is now a regular page in the sidebar. Add a provider from a catalog, then set its key, who can use it and which models in one form. Overview shows who spends what and on which models, with a page for each person. Limits lets you cap spend per day, week or month for everyone, a team or one person, and you can undo a deleted limit. Users & Teams shows everyone's providers, limits and last 31 days of spend. Mistral is now supported. Members can sign in to Gemini and Claude on Google Cloud with their own Google account from the new Models section of My Library, which replaces the old My Model Connections page.
  • Connectors and plugins are simpler to manage. For admins in OpenWork Cloud: add a connector in a few steps, choose whether each person signs in or one account is shared by everyone, and pick which teams get it. Add any MCP adds a server that isn't in the catalog, or you can paste its address into the search. Manage › Plugins lists every plugin with who has it. You can create one and give it to teams right there, then search by name or filter by team or person. Removing a connector or plugin now asks first, and switching a connector to one shared account warns you before it signs you out. Owners can also approve their self-hosted OpenWork web address in Org settings so members can sign in there, even if they belong to several organizations.
  • Also in this release. The first time you click a link, OpenWork asks whether to open it in OpenWork or your usual browser and can remember your choice. You can change it later in Settings › Preferences › Browser, or right-click a link to choose once. Session search and notifications sit next to the OpenWork name at the top of the sidebar, and window controls look native on macOS, Windows and Linux. The built-in browser no longer has a Suspend button. After you sign in, Settings › AI providers works right away, even before you create your first workspace. openwork.summary: Run OpenWork on your own server with one command Self-host OpenWork with one command. For self-hosters: npm i -g openwork-server && openwork-server web now runs the full OpenWork web app on a home server or VPS. It downloads the matching engine on first run…
openwork.html:
Run OpenWork on your own server with one command

  • Self-host OpenWork with one command. For self-hosters: npm i -g openwork-server && openwork-server web now runs the full OpenWork web app on a home server or VPS. It downloads the matching engine on first run and keeps its access tokens across restarts, and npm i -g openwork-server@latest updates it. Before, you had to clone and build the repo, install the engine yourself, and recreate tokens after every restart.
  • Connecting an account in chat no longer gets stuck. When the agent needs you to connect a service, you now always get a clear card to connect or skip, with Try again if sign-in doesn't finish. Before, chat could wait forever on "Checking connection request…".
  • Chat replies are simpler. Creating or sharing a skill, asking for a mockup, being asked for an environment variable, and browsing connectors now reply in plain text instead of embedded cards. The connection card is the only one that stays.
  • Your email stays out of the sidebar. The account row now shows your name and "OpenWork Cloud" instead of your email address. Your email is still at the top of the account menu.
  • If you use OpenWork from Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex: agents can now list your organization's skills and open any of them directly. Before, they had to guess search keywords, so organization skills often went unused.
  • Clearer pricing everywhere. The website, docs, and sign-up now all show the same plans: Free, Team at $10 per seat per month, and Enterprise at $40 per user billed annually, with Cloud Computer and OpenWork models as add-ons. The website and docs also have refreshed branding.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.9
emdash.summary: This release adds GitLab repository and merge request workflows, with browser and device sign-in for GitLab.com. It also adds support for Apple silicon Mac remotes and improves terminal links, account reconnection, and project dialogs. Highlights Create GitLab…
emdash.html:
This release adds GitLab repository and merge request workflows, with browser and device sign-in for GitLab.com. It also adds support for Apple silicon Mac remotes and improves terminal links, account reconnection, and project dialogs.

Highlights
  • Create GitLab repositories in personal namespaces or existing groups, including nested groups, and publish an existing project through Add Remote. Connected self-hosted instances are supported, and task creation uses GitLab's work-item terminology.
  • Browse, create, and merge GitLab merge requests from Emdash. View approvals, pipeline jobs, discussions, commits, and changed files, mark drafts ready, and start or review tasks from merge requests, including those from forks.
  • Connect GitLab.com through your Emdash account or with a device code, with automatic token renewal. Device sign-in stays inside the connection dialog with copy, open, retry, and cancel controls. Self-hosted GitLab instances continue to use access tokens.
  • Remote workspace server installation now supports Apple silicon Macs using the tools included with macOS. Terminal sessions on those hosts start correctly after installation.
Fixes
  • Wrapped terminal hyperlinks open their full destination, including links printed by Claude Code. Copy Link uses the hyperlink's destination or joins lines wrapped by the terminal, while normal selection copying preserves line breaks and keeps separate URLs apart.
  • Clicking a terminal hyperlink opens it locally without also asking the remote agent to launch a browser. Link handling preserves text selection and cancels pending clicks when dragging or switching focus. IPv6 URLs retain their closing brackets.
  • Long directory paths stay within project dialogs, keeping the directory chooser visible at narrow window widths.
  • Add Remote creates an empty repository before publishing the current branch, preserving existing history. Repository creation, fetching, and publishing consistently use the selected account.
  • Creating a task from a branch opens the workspace settings directly, with no issue or merge request preselected.
  • GitLab merge request reviews recover missing commits from the correct source, including fork merge requests. Refreshing the merge request list retains cached details, and unavailable diff counts remain unknown instead of appearing as zero.
  • Expiring integration credentials renew before Git operations use them. Tokens replaced on another device are refreshed after rejection, and temporary renewal failures can be retried.
  • Reconnecting preserves the selected account, and background token renewal cannot restore a disconnected account or overwrite a newer connection. Cancelled device sign-in saves nothing, and newly issued tokens are retried if the provider briefly rejects them.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.8
emdash.summary: This release adds language intelligence to the editor, subscription usage meters, and YouTrack integration. It also brings diff comments to chat and improves file browsing, agent status, and desktop integration. Highlights The editor adds hover information,…
emdash.html:
This release adds language intelligence to the editor, subscription usage meters, and YouTrack integration. It also brings diff comments to chat and improves file browsing, agent status, and desktop integration.

Highlights
  • The editor adds hover information, definitions, type definitions, references, and diagnostics for local and SSH workspaces. JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python language servers are bundled; additional servers support Bash, Go, Rust, C/C++, JSON, YAML, HTML, and CSS dialects. Language service status and restart controls are available in the file tab menu.
  • A new Usage page in settings shows remaining Codex and Claude Code subscription allowances, reset countdowns, and refresh controls. Shared accounts appear once across machines, and stale or unavailable readings are clearly marked.
  • Connect YouTrack Cloud or self-hosted instances with a permanent token, search tickets using YouTrack queries, and start tasks with ticket descriptions and comments. Ticket context includes up to the latest 100 accessible comments and uses readable ticket identifiers.
  • Attach draft diff comments to chat through the “Diff comments” item in the @ menu. Comments are cleared only after confirmed delivery, while failed sends and comments edited during submission remain pending.
  • Jira setup now offers a choice between email and API token or a manually supplied bearer access token.
  • Branch Commits can switch between a flat file list and a nested tree, with its own saved view preference.
Fixes
  • File browsing shares live folder listings across views and updates changed folders without rebuilding the entire tree. Folder expansion, drag-hover, and new-file placement are more reliable, names sort naturally, and files named __proto__ remain visible and editable.
  • Language services preserve unsaved edits across restarts and reconnects. Built-in editor support remains available where supported when a language server is unavailable, and language service or usage worker failures no longer block host startup.
  • Switching back to a task keeps terminal and agent dimensions in sync, preventing misplaced cursors, clipped lines, and overdrawn frames. Hidden panes no longer produce invalid terminal grid sizes.
  • Cursor and OpenCode working indicators clear correctly when agents finish or stop, including OpenCode sessions using custom providers. Chat resumes its working indicator after permission approval and ignores late prompt results after a session closes.
  • Chat preserves prices, literal HTML and XML, and inline math source instead of hiding text or showing empty message cards. Claude monitor events appear as passive notifications without interrupting active turns or duplicating screen-reader output.
  • Hidden issue and review context stays out of replayed chat transcripts. Draft diff comments remain visible when switching files or when the editor finishes loading.
  • SSH connections support OpenSSH user certificates supplied by the SSH agent. Reconnection logs include the underlying error instead of an unreadable object value.
  • Installed-app detection on macOS avoids application chooser prompts and recognizes GUI-only apps. Failed checks can be retried, and Windows detection respects custom installation directories.
  • Opening remote workspaces in VS Code, VSCodium, or Cursor requests a new window. “Open in Terminal” on Linux tries the user's default terminal before falling back to common terminal applications.
  • Merge commits show files changed against their first parent. Project and workspace inspection preserve Git errors instead of treating failed repository checks as ordinary directories.
  • Agent installation shows all supported options for the current platform, including WinGet for Claude Code on Windows.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.7
emdash.summary: This release remembers agent settings across tasks, adds native provider controls to the chat composer, and improves session recovery. It also makes update downloads, project opening, and conversation navigation more reliable. Highlights Chat remembers your…
emdash.html:
This release remembers agent settings across tasks, adds native provider controls to the chat composer, and improves session recovery. It also makes update downloads, project opening, and conversation navigation more reliable.

Highlights
  • Chat remembers your model, effort, access mode, and other provider settings across tasks and projects, with separate preferences for each agent and machine. New automations inherit these preferences and retain their own saved settings for scheduled runs.
  • Switch between Chat UI and TUI directly in the agent selector. Your interface choice is remembered across agents, projects, and machines.
  • Task creation and active chat use the provider's available configuration options, including a fast-mode toggle where supported. Chat permissions follow the provider's native access mode, and TUI auto-approval is remembered separately.
  • Claude's model picker adds Opus 5.5, and Codex adds GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Model choices use the identifiers supported by each agent so selections carry through to the session correctly.
Fixes
  • Missing ACP sessions can be retried or replaced with a fresh session in the same conversation, preserving drafts and selected settings. Sessions that never started recover automatically when the provider confirms they are missing.
  • Initial prompts survive failed startup preparation and worker restarts. Transcripts remain visible while sessions reconnect and reload their history.
  • Cached composer settings remain visible during startup, and failed preference saves show a warning. Changing shared preferences leaves existing conversations and saved automations unchanged.
  • Notification clicks focus or reopen the correct conversation tab, including chats in another pane, without creating a blank terminal tab.
  • Update downloads keep their progress when navigating away from settings or when a request times out. Failures show readable messages, retry controls, and expandable diagnostics that can be copied with credentials redacted.
  • Agent discovery avoids repeated checks, and local project opening retries temporary timeouts. Cancelled or failed initialization cleans up background work without interrupting existing task sessions.
  • Imports from v0 preserve workspace paths, remote conversation locations, and valid Claude session resume information.
  • File links in chat open the editor at the referenced line number.
  • POSIX paths retain forward-slash separators and preserve literal backslashes in filenames.
  • CSV previews retain an empty quoted row at the end of a file, even without a trailing newline.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.6
emdash.summary: This release restores file drops and image pastes in remote terminals, adds OpenCode v2 status support, and detects IPv6 preview servers. It also improves search results, agent session restoration, and desktop integration. Highlights Drop local files or paste…
emdash.html:
This release restores file drops and image pastes in remote terminals, adds OpenCode v2 status support, and detects IPv6 preview servers. It also improves search results, agent session restoration, and desktop integration.

Highlights
  • Drop local files or paste images into remote agent terminals and shells. Files upload to the machine running the session before their paths are inserted, with progress and error feedback.
  • OpenCode v2 reports working, completion, and error status through native hooks. Interrupted runs return to idle, and session tracking remains compatible with earlier OpenCode versions.
  • Preview detection recognizes IPv6 loopback URLs such as http://[::1]:3000, with correctly formatted links in the preview server list.
Fixes
  • File drops into Claude Code terminals retain the full path instead of leaving only a space. Image pastes avoid duplicate attachments, and pending transfers are cancelled when their target pane or session changes.
  • Stored attachments remain available across session shutdowns, workspace deactivation, and restarts without expiring by age. Incomplete uploads are cleaned up after crashes, and deleting a conversation or workspace also cleans up its stored attachments.
  • Antigravity resumes the correct native conversation instead of starting a fresh session with a “conversation not found” warning.
  • Search removes duplicate and stale results for projects, tasks, and conversations. Deleting a project also removes its tasks and conversations from search.
  • Commit file lists and working-tree diffs preserve filenames containing Unicode, quotes, tabs, or other special characters, including renamed and copied files.
  • The in-app browser keeps a successfully loaded page visible when an embedded iframe fails to load.
  • Remote workspace creation retries failed home-directory lookups after a host reconnects, avoiding persistent “unusable runtime” errors.
  • macOS Option-arrow shortcuts retain their native behavior in terminal agents while shell panes keep word navigation.
  • Linux launcher and window identities match correctly on Wayland and X11, keeping dock grouping consistent and preserving existing pins for stable and canary builds.
  • Agent settings and the agent selector show installation guide links, and link icons are placed consistently.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.5
emdash.summary: This release adds multiple accounts per integration, custom agent executable selection, and more control over the workbench. It also makes ACP conversations, task archiving, and remote connections more reliable. Highlights Connect multiple accounts for each…
emdash.html:
This release adds multiple accounts per integration, custom agent executable selection, and more control over the workbench. It also makes ACP conversations, task archiving, and remote connections more reliable.

Highlights
  • Connect multiple accounts for each integration, choose a default, and select which account each project uses. Account choices carry through project creation, issue browsing, and pull request workflows.
  • Choose an agent executable by path or command name in settings, validate it before saving, and use that selection when launching agents. Custom wrapper scripts are supported, including PowerShell wrappers on Windows.
  • Hide the Emdash menu bar or system tray icon from Interface settings.
  • Newly opened file diffs scroll directly to the first change, while previously viewed diffs retain their saved position.
  • Codex adds a curl installation option on macOS and Linux, and MCP startup failures appear in the chat composer's server list with error details.
Fixes
  • ACP transcripts keep pending prompts and live responses visible as turns finish and history loads. Scroll position and session settings survive history refreshes, and background agent events update the correct turn.
  • Failed session restores preserve saved conversations and show recoverable errors. Agent sign-in remains accessible, and terminal startup failures no longer disrupt the ACP worker.
  • Each conversation retains its prompt draft, text selection, undo history, and composer scroll position when switching tabs. Empty chats keep the composer centered during startup.
  • Archiving runs teardown scripts when possible and remains available when a remote host is offline. Restoring archived tasks works across repeated archive and restore cycles, and cleanup state stays consistent across restarts.
  • Workspace lookup uses current saved state, avoiding stale “workspace not found” errors. Conversation lists recover after missed updates, and closing a conversation tab clears its attention indicator.
  • Pull request details refresh reliably after runtime recovery, and CI results stay tied to the current commit. Staged and unstaged file lists remain stable during background Git updates.
  • SSH-config connections allow authentication and private key overrides. Testing and saving use the same credentials, and saved passwords and passphrases are reused only for the matching connection or key.
  • Routine remote connection checks no longer cause status flicker or interrupt terminal input. Git credentials also remain available to child processes, including editor extensions.
  • Muse Code and Antigravity report working and completion status through native hooks. Codex approval settings parse correctly on Windows, and Devin handles compound shell commands correctly.
  • macOS Option-arrow shortcuts navigate shell words correctly, and tmux startup handles terminal capability queries more reliably.
  • Localhost links offer the usual choice to open in Emdash or an external browser. Pane focus preserves scroll position, sidebar task reordering stays accurate after auto-scroll, and panels remain clickable over the title bar.
  • Project opening failures show actionable errors, including invalid remote default branches. Crash recovery also offers an explicit option to reset saved UI state and reload.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.4
emdash.summary: This release makes ACP conversations easier to follow and more reliable to use, especially across remote reconnections. It also adds Muse Code, project renaming, and several agent and provider improvements. Highlights Agent activity is easier to scan: related…
emdash.html:
This release makes ACP conversations easier to follow and more reliable to use, especially across remote reconnections. It also adds Muse Code, project renaming, and several agent and provider improvements.

Highlights
  • Agent activity is easier to scan: related thinking blocks are grouped, consecutive tool calls collapse into “Ran N commands,” and command rows use compact, descriptive headings.
  • Rename projects directly from the project header or sidebar menu.
  • Muse Code is now available as a coding agent, and CodeBuddy Code adds lifecycle hooks for accurate status, session, error, and permission notifications.
  • Codex adds GPT-6 Astra to its model options, and OpenCode can connect to OrcaRouter as a named OpenAI-compatible provider.
  • The chat composer now shows the selected model effort beside the model name.
Fixes
  • Prompt queuing works correctly while an ACP agent is active. Drafts are preserved across tab changes and delivery failures, and prompts clear only after the agent accepts them.
  • Remote projects and conversations recover more reliably after sleep, network interruptions, and workspace-server reconnects. Transcript history reloads correctly, and connection status remains stable during recovery.
  • Terminal and TUI-agent sessions use readable, identity-backed tmux names and recover the correct process more reliably, including after idle periods.
  • Pull request status refreshes consistently, repositories are polled every minute, and requested or startup-failed CI checks are classified correctly.
  • External symlink targets can be browsed in the file tree, while diff buffers remain read-only and file references from agent transcripts open at the reported line.
  • SSH connections respect filtered agent identities, and macOS can request local-network access when connecting to machines over LAN SSH.
  • Project migrations handle legacy workspace identity conflicts without interrupting registry sync.
  • The in-app browser favicon, external-link dialog, task-tab cursor, collapsed plans, and prompt-editor links now behave consistently.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.3
emdash.summary: This release adds Prime Agent, project-level environment variables, drag-to-split panes, and native Linux ARM64 builds. It also refreshes the workbench and file tree while improving file watching, search, and restored sessions. Highlights Prime Agent is now…
emdash.html:
This release adds Prime Agent, project-level environment variables, drag-to-split panes, and native Linux ARM64 builds. It also refreshes the workbench and file tree while improving file watching, search, and restored sessions.

Highlights
  • Prime Agent is now available as a coding agent, with native ACP chat, resumable sessions, MCP servers, and Emdash hooks.
  • Define environment variables in project settings and apply them consistently to agents, terminals, and lifecycle scripts.
  • Drag a tab to any edge of a pane to create a split and place it there. Tab bars and the terminal drawer also have a cleaner, flatter design.
  • The file explorer now carries Git status colors up to parent folders, making changed files easier to locate.
  • Claude adds Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 support.
  • Native Linux packages are now built for both x64 and ARM64 in AppImage, DEB, and RPM formats.
Fixes
  • File search and file watching recover more reliably from failed or cancelled watchers, honor exclusion settings, and avoid holding inactive workspaces open.
  • Git repositories remain usable if a watcher cannot attach, and repository scans do less redundant work.
  • Restored terminal-agent sessions recover correctly after an app restart.
  • Markdown reference links and images render correctly, and wide tables can scroll horizontally.
  • The chat composer keeps the caret visible across line breaks, while mention and other selection popovers stay within the viewport.
  • Project directory browsing, task-specific sidebar widths, terminal theme changes, and empty terminal drawers now behave consistently.
  • Linux secure storage is configured before startup, and Windows agent launching prefers the correct executable shim.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.2
emdash.summary: This release adds Plan mode to Codex chat and improves remote development over Tailscale SSH, along with more reliable agent launching on Windows. Highlights Codex ACP conversations can switch between Default and Plan modes directly from the chat composer,…
emdash.html:
This release adds Plan mode to Codex chat and improves remote development over Tailscale SSH, along with more reliable agent launching on Windows.

Highlights
  • Codex ACP conversations can switch between Default and Plan modes directly from the chat composer, with the selection remembered across sessions.
Fixes
  • Remote workspaces can connect over Tailscale SSH now that Unix socket forwarding works with compatible servers that use a non-OpenSSH identification banner.
  • Windows preserves native command lines when launching .cmd agent shims, so agents such as Pi start correctly when arguments contain spaces or quotes.
  • Saved ACP configuration options are cleared when an agent no longer supports them, preventing stale selections from being reapplied.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.1
emdash.summary: This small release focuses on reliability across remote development, Windows, and agent sessions. Fixes Remote ACP prompts no longer time out while an agent is working, and successfully delivered prompts no longer show a false failure or return to the…
emdash.html:
This small release focuses on reliability across remote development, Windows, and agent sessions.

Fixes
  • Remote ACP prompts no longer time out while an agent is working, and successfully delivered prompts no longer show a false failure or return to the composer.
  • Large prompts and dropped files are stored on the target machine so remote agents can access them reliably.
  • Windows project activation now handles drive-letter and UNC paths, with more reliable agent launching, shell detection, and process cleanup.
  • Workspace, worktree, and file paths are handled consistently on Windows, including directory selection, file opening, links, and symlinks.
  • The remote project directory picker stays responsive and no longer repeats loading cycles while navigating.
  • Project settings are preserved through transient read failures, and worktrees are no longer modified with Emdash-specific state.

emdash.title: Emdash v1.2.0
emdash.summary: This release introduces the new Emdash Workspace Server, bringing remote development much closer to the local Emdash experience. It also adds per-machine management for agent resources, file-content search, faster task creation, and a more capable and reliable…
emdash.html:
This release introduces the new Emdash Workspace Server, bringing remote development much closer to the local Emdash experience. It also adds per-machine management for agent resources, file-content search, faster task creation, and a more capable and reliable chat UI for ACP agents.

Highlights
  • The Emdash Workspace Server brings remote projects on par with local development, including Git, files, terminals, agents, automations, file search, and preview forwarding.
  • Manage each machine independently, including its workspaces, conversations, agents, MCP servers, skills, dependencies, and resource usage.
  • Search file contents from the task sidebar with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F, jump directly to matching lines, and automatically reveal opened files in the file tree.
  • Tasks open faster, with non-blocking setup work continuing in the background. A new Activity menu shows worktree setup and lifecycle-script progress.
  • The ACP chat UI now keeps drafts and attachments across navigation and delivery failures, restores suspended conversations without disrupting chat, and remembers provider and session options.
Everything else
  • Open an existing workspace in a task instead of creating a new worktree.
  • Sort project tasks by last used or creation time.
  • Rename conversations and select multiple conversations for deletion.
  • The command palette now searches commands, files, conversations, projects, and tasks, while Settings has its own searchable navigation.
  • CodeBuddy is available as a coding agent, Claude adds Opus 5 while retaining Opus 4.8, and agent selectors show clearer capability icons.
  • PhpStorm is available in the Open In menu.
  • Project settings show where a new worktree will be created, and long lists such as Git remotes are searchable.
  • The app shows its window and branded loading state sooner, includes better startup recovery, and adds a system tray icon.
  • Project expansion preferences persist across restarts, and expanded projects use the open-folder icon.
Fixes
  • Pull request detection stays stable across refreshes and matches the exact head branch; staging remains responsive, diff paths stay checkout-relative, and branch commits no longer flicker.
  • Editor and diff scroll positions survive tab and task switches, the commit input no longer steals focus, and file reveal operations no longer time out during tree refreshes.
  • Chat execution text no longer clips, search labels are no longer duplicated, raw search queries are preserved, and file links open in the adjacent editor pane.
  • Sidebar shortcuts expand collapsed panels and keep working through overlays; the theme command is restored to the command palette.
  • New-task settings and GitHub identity details fit correctly in the modal, and auto-approve preferences persist.
  • Remote projects behave more reliably across reconnects and relinks, recover failed file watchers, and publish branches to the correct remote.
  • Terminal processes receive the user's environment without leaking worker settings, and terminal QR codes render without line gaps.
  • Windows title bars follow the app theme, and agent hooks work correctly on Windows.
  • Codex notifications and device authentication work again, and provider environment variables are applied correctly to ACP sessions.
  • Automation controls, project and settings layouts, markdown checkbox contrast, and other interface details have been polished.

Emdash v1.1.27 is out! emdash.html:
Emdash v1.1.25 is out! This release improves PR and task workflows, adds better terminal and diff-view support (including Windows paste, image paste persistence, and TSX/JSX highlighting), expands compatibility with GitHub Enterprise remotes, and includes a new MCP provider (Notra) plus a range of performance, stability, and UI polish fixes.

  • feat(mcp): add Notra server by @mezotv in https://github.com/generalaction/emdash/pull/2190

emdash.html:
Emdash v1.1.24 is out!

This release brings major improvements to SSH and remote workflows (including ProxyJump, ProxyCommand, ForwardAgent, and better MaxSessions handling), a more polished navigation and sidebar experience, better task and PR flows, expanded terminal/open-in-app support, new integrations and providers (Neon, Antigravity, Asana polish), plus a long list of stability, performance, editor, and UI fixes across the app.

Emdash v1.1.10 is out!

Emdash v1.1.5

Emdash v1 is now stable.

This release builds on the v1 launch with a set of fixes, performance improvements, and groundwork for upcoming features like remote workflows and BYOI workspaces.

If you're upgrading from v0.4.x, you can import your existing tasks during onboarding.

Changes since v0.27.0:

Summary

This is a major feature release packed with exciting improvements! 🎉

🚀 Major New Capabilities:

  • GPT-5 Support - Works with OpenAI's latest model
  • Claude 4 Support - Works with Anthropic's latest model
  • MCP Integration 🔌 - Support for Model Context Protocol servers, expanding tool ecosystem

🤖 Agent & Automation Enhancements:

  • Auto-commit - Automatically tell agent to git commit, or do it manually with /commit
  • Custom Agent Improvements - Even better support for agents based on the gptme-agent-template
  • Agent Workspace Auto-detection - Smarter handling of agent environments

🛠 Tool Improvements:

  • Shell Timeouts ⏱️ - Configurable command timeouts (set GPTME_SHELL_TIMEOUT)
  • Morph Tool ✨ - Alternative fast patching tool for precise code edits
  • Perplexity Search 🔍 - Enhanced web search capabilities through the browser tool
  • Computer Tool Improvements 💻 - Better key sequence chaining for GUI automation
  • Enhanced TTS 🗣️ - Improved text-to-speech with Chatterbox support

🌐 Server & API:

  • Redesigned Server API - Complete API overhaul for better web UI integration
  • Tasks API - New task management capabilities
  • OpenAPI Specification - Comprehensive API documentation

🔧 Quality of Life:

  • Setup Command ⚙️ - Easy configuration with /setup
  • 90+ Bug Fixes - Significantly improved stability and reliability
  • Better Configuration - Enhanced config system with user-, project-, and chat-specific settings
  • Improved Error Handling - More user-friendly error messages and recovery
  • Bell and Tool Sounds 🔊 - Pleasant notification sounds for user input requested and different operations (enable via /setup or GPTME_DING/GPTME_TOOL_SOUNDS env vars)

These are the release notes for gptme version v0.27.0.

Contributors

Thanks to everyone who contributed to this release:

@0xbrayo, @erikbjare, @jrmi, @Miyou

✨ Summary

This release brings a wealth of exciting improvements and new capabilities to gptme:

🚀 Major Enhancements

  • 🔧 Pre-commit Integration: Automatically run pre-commit hooks when tool use is exhausted, keeping your code clean and consistent!
  • 🍎 macOS Computer Use Tool: Extended our powerful computer use tool to macOS users, allowing the assistant to interact with GUI applications
  • 🧠 Reasoning Models Better Supported:
    • Claude 3.7 Sonnet support
    • DeepSeek R1 support
  • 🔈 Improved TTS: Enhanced Text-to-Speech with Kokoro 1.0, better sentence chunking and device handling

🛠️ Developer Experience

  • 🌳 Context Tree: Added GPTME_CONTEXT_TREE flag to include repository structure in prompts
  • ⚙️ Feature Flags: New environment variables like GPTME_BREAK_ON_TOOLUSE and GPTME_FRESH for advanced users
  • 🔍 Enhanced RAG: Much improved document retrieval with LLM post-processing
  • 📊 Terminal Status: Real-time status updates in terminal title
  • 🔄 Auto-rename: Added script to intelligently rename past conversations

🔧 Under the Hood

  • 🐛 Bug Fixes: Fixed 65+ issues to ensure smooth, reliable operation
  • 📷 Better Image Handling: Improved vision tool with automatic rescaling
  • 📋 Model Switching: Added /model command to list and switch models in conversation
  • 🔄 Patch Recovery: New GPTME_PATCH_RECOVERY option to recover from non-matching patches

We apologize for the delay in this release. For those eager to try the latest features before the next release, we recommend running directly from the master branch:

pipx install git+https://github.com/gptme/gptme.git

These are the release notes for gptme version v0.25.0.

Summary

This release brings major improvements to the user experience with a new prompt_toolkit-based interface (better completion and highlighting), support for OpenAI/Anthropic tools APIs, and significant cost & performance improvements for Anthropic through better prompt caching. The release also includes improved path handling, workspace context, heredoc support, and numerous UX improvements and bug fixes.

These are the release notes for gptme version v0.14.0.

Contributors

Thanks to everyone who contributed to this release:

@erikbjare

Changelog

Changes since v0.13.2:

📦 gptme

✨ Features (2)
  • feat: anthropic prompt caching beta (bb3d9a5)
  • feat: started working on vision (7b0c5b0)
🐛 Fixes (25)
Click to expand

  • fix: improved test flakiness (0758c4d)
  • fix: check if gitignore exists (d664f4b)
  • fix: moved vue@create example into bash tool (dont try to do it interactively) (5ed36eb)
  • fix: switch to ```ipython syntax for executing with python tool, to differentiate from code samples (see #67) (42ee56a)
  • fix: changed save format to be more explicit (68077b6)
  • fix: removed spammy warning (90aa4a6)
  • fix: removed use of NotRequired for TypedDict (not in Python 3.10) (cfce130)
  • fix: use anthropic api max_retries instead of custom retry_anthropic decorator (008f58c)
  • fix: added retry_anthropic decorator for rate limits (d37d7fb)
  • fix: fixed to evals, capture eval output on timeout/terminate (cd0862a)
  • fix: fixed spammy prints (855a46b)
  • fix: clarified return format for subagent (e5e2a9a)
  • fix: fixed bug in transform_examples_to_chat_directives (2997aa4)
  • fix: print logs dir with --version command (1ca6127)
  • fix: enabled stricter linting and fixed lints (apparently needed given a25aa7d369dec79341500bcf735e4237def53052) (bf67b32)
  • fix: fixed nasty bug with mutable argument default (a25aa7d)
  • fix: switch recommended openai model to gpt-4o (b3582ac)
  • fix: moved len_tokens and msgs2dicts from util.py to message.py (94bade3)
  • fix: support nested codeblocks, rewrote/refactored codeblock parsing/management (3e291a4)
  • fix: fixed incorrect storage format for Message.to_dict (07f1cbb)
  • fix: added preliminary nested codeblock support (885e544)
  • fix: added openai vision support (6bbec93)
  • fix: completed basic vision support (f184607)
  • fix: correct extremely short 'Thinking...' message, now wait until first character (b25e576)
  • fix: typing for subagent tool, added --check-untypes-defs to mypy (d94a71e)

🔨 Misc (20)
Click to expand

  • chore: bumped version to v0.14.0 (d4c55b6)
  • refactor: renamed terminal tool to tmux (79355bc)
  • tests: increase max tokens for full system prompt significantly (c785cfe)
  • tests: made test_subprocess less flaky (3423474)
  • tests: added difficult but reasonably simple integration test example (create vite project, build simple app) (57b6feb)
  • docs(README): minor improvements (c43cc8a)
  • docs(README): misc minor improvements (c705c80)
  • tests: removed uninteresting examples from test-integration.sh (18c1afa)
  • docs: added links to top of README (b15d686)
  • docs(README): added mention that vision works, 'GPTMe' -> 'gptme' for title, mention OpenRouter support (4e39f63)
  • tests: run both eval tests (cli and direct call) for better coverage somehow (859efbe)
  • tests: fixed tests failing due to new file (706f13c)
  • refactor: refactored provider-specific code into new files llm_openai.py and llm_anthropic.py (eec8215)
  • tests: fix coverage for eval tests (multiprocessing workaround) (9ef1ec4)
  • tests: added test_eval_cli and cleaned up eval code (c0e5c87)
  • tests: basic test for evals (770ed2c)
  • tests: fix --version test (4ca5078)
  • tests: remove ambiguity in subagent fib test prompt (fe063ec)
  • tests: added test for vision (a740194)
  • refactor: moved eval code into gptme.eval, added gptme-eval entrypoint, fixed typing (8a1bb09)

claude-squad.html:
Claude Squad v1.0.0

Claude Squad is a terminal app lets you manage multiple Claude Code (and other local agents like Aider) instances across separate workspaces, so you can tackle multiple tasks at once.

  • Run tasks in the background (with yolo/auto-accept mode)
  • Control all instances and tasks from one terminal window
  • Review changes before applying, checkout before pushing
  • Isolated git workspaces per task—no more conflicts!

mini-swe-agent.summary: [!warning] This is the first full release of mini-swe-agent v2. This includes lots of breaking changes. This is the largest new release since the launch, focusing on supporting more diverse models and switching to toolcalls by default (as opposed to manual…
mini-swe-agent.html:
[!warning] This is the first full release of mini-swe-agent v2. This includes lots of breaking changes.

This is the largest new release since the launch, focusing on supporting more diverse models and switching to toolcalls by default (as opposed to manual parsing of actions).

What's new?

  • Tool calls: Native tool calling API is now the support, text-based action parsing is still available
  • Multimodal input: Support for images and other content types
  • More flexible model support in general

What do I need to change?

I only use the mini CLI with default configs

No changes needed.

I use custom configs

You might need to move some config keys. See Config changes.

I parse/analyze trajectories

Some metadata fields moved to extra. See Trajectory format.

I use the python bindings or built custom subclasses

You will need to refactor. An agent can refactor your code based on the instructions below.

Full migration guide

Read the full migration guide.

Changes compared to v2.0.0a3:

  • Enable parallel tool calls and use plain text observation template by @aorwall in https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/pull/722

mini-swe-agent.html:
This release introduces changes to how we handle Anthropic models, in particular with respect to caching. These are mostly internal changes, it is unlikely that you need to change anything on your end. The advantage is that you can now use Anthropic models also with other "backends" like portkey rather than having to use the litellm class.

Here's the breakdown of the changes:

  1. Simpler cache breakpoint setting: We only apply one cache breakpoint at the end
  2. If no model class is specified Anthropic models are also handled by litellm
  3. All model classes apply the cache breakpoints automatically if the model name suggest an Anthropic model, unless the set_cache_control option is explicitly set to None
  4. Anthropic key rotation is deprecated (as are some minor internal methods)

Changed

  • Change: Anthropic caching applied at end; deprecate cache-related options by @klieret in https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/pull/570
  • Change: Use litellm class for anthropic; cache control support by @klieret in https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent/pull/571
